Constraint Handling Rules (CHR) is a declarative, logic-based language designed for constraint solving, featuring multiple heads per rule that allow for parallel execution. This paper examines the expressive power of CHR programs with respect to their ability to solve problems, specifically analyzing the limits imposed by a fixed number of rule heads. We demonstrate that even with a constant number of heads, CHR can solve any decision problem solvable within polynomial time, a capability that extends to problems solvable in linear time when the number of heads scales logarithmically with input size. Furthermore, we establish that CHR cannot solve NP-complete problems unless P equals NP. These findings are derived from a novel characterization of the complexity classes definable by CHR programs with a fixed number of heads, a result achieved through the introduction of a new class of circuit families.

Meta-learning has recently demonstrated significant success in adapting to new tasks with limited data. However, current methods often fail to generalize effectively when faced with noisy labels or sampling errors. To address this, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a new approach that leverages the spectral properties of the Reptile matrix to identify a robust shared representation across multiple tasks. This method is then adapted to specific tasks using a combination of label smoothing and self-training. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets reveal that Eigen-Reptile outperforms existing meta-learning techniques, achieving up to a 10% improvement in accuracy under noisy label conditions and a 5% gain under noisy sampling conditions.

We introduce a new machine learning framework designed to generate interpretable predictions for individual brain scans, specifically for detecting neurological phenotypes. This system utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract feature attributions, which are then processed by a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to produce final classifications. The GNN incorporates a specialized mechanism that leverages the inherent spatial structure of the feature attributions to enhance interpretability. Experimental results on a dataset of 1,000 individuals with Multiple Sclerosis demonstrate that this approach achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while offering significant interpretability advantages.

AI ethics has been a prominent field of study for some time, yet it has predominantly concentrated on specific issues. This paper examines the marginalization of certain groups within AI ethics by analyzing the work of the prominent scholar Annika Lindgren. By applying a feminist lens, the study highlights how women and other marginalized groups are overlooked in this field. The analysis reveals that while the issue of AI ethics has gained significant attention, the focus remains disproportionately on certain topics while neglecting others. This paper argues that the marginalization of women and other groups in AI ethics is a result of the field's failure to consider the diverse perspectives and experiences of all members of society.

$\omega$-regular languages constitute a crucial class of languages defined over infinite words, serving as a cornerstone for numerous theoretical analyses and practical applications. This paper investigates the extension of these languages to infinite words drawn from a broader alphabet. We demonstrate that when extending the alphabet of $\omega$-regular languages, the resulting languages remain $\omega$-regular. Furthermore, we introduce a specific construction method to generate such languages and establish that $\omega$-regularity is preserved under the extension operation.

This study introduces a deep learning (DL) framework for estimating channel states in cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems, addressing the challenges posed by channel aging and frequent channel estimation. The proposed method utilizes a hybrid approach combining alternating channel estimation and prediction. Specifically, the system employs a long-term prediction model to forecast channel states for users that have not been recently estimated, while using short-term estimation for those estimated recently. The core of this architecture is a Deep Neural Network (DNN) that learns the relationship between channel states of recently estimated users and those of all users, enabling accurate prediction of the latter based on the former. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DL-based scheme significantly outperforms conventional channel estimation techniques, achieving superior accuracy with reduced computational complexity.

We examine the semileptonic radiative corrections governing the semileptonic decay of the neutron, $n \to p e^- \bar{\nu}_e$, with a specific focus on the correction term $g_{\rm{EWT}}$ within the standard model's effective weak coupling constant, $G_{\rm{V}} = G_{\rm{F}}(1 + \Delta_{\rm{R}})$. This correction accounts for short-distance QED effects and is derived from the renormalization of the vector current. We demonstrate that the current approach to calculating $g_{\rm{EWT}}$ relies on the renormalization constant $Z_{\rm{V}}$ for the vector current. Furthermore, we outline how this quantity can be determined using lattice QCD and provide an updated estimate of $g_{\rm{EWT}}$ based on recent lattice computations.

This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework for image denoising grounded in the concept of additive white Gaussian noise. The proposed architecture leverages a residual structure, where the core mechanism involves the network learning to predict the residual noise map. This map is subsequently added to a feature representation of the clean image to reconstruct the final denoised output. To enhance performance, we incorporate identity preservation losses that compel the network to retain essential semantic information from the clean image during the denoising process. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both PSNR and SSIM metrics.

Correlated latent variables are prevalent in numerous machine learning applications, including multiview learning and self-supervised learning. This study investigates the identifiability of these latent variables within a specific generative model. We demonstrate that under mild conditions, the joint distribution of these latents can be uniquely identified up to specific linear transformations, provided the number of views or tasks is sufficiently large. Furthermore, we examine the implications of this theoretical framework for learning latents in practical scenarios.

We introduce a novel method for identifying star-forming galaxies that are heavily obscured by dust, utilizing the mid-infrared (MIR) colours of the WISE W1-W2 and W2-W3 bands. This approach is grounded in the observation that the MIR colours of star-forming galaxies are significantly redder than those of quiescent galaxies, a trend driven by the presence of warm dust heated by active star formation. By applying this technique to the SDSS-DR12 sample, we identified a sample of 1,000 star-forming galaxies with exceptionally red MIR colours. These galaxies are characterized by high dust attenuation, elevated star formation rates, and a prevalence of starbursts. Furthermore, we examined the MIR properties of these galaxies using the Herschel-ATLAS sample, revealing that they are more luminous in the far-infrared (FIR) and exhibit higher dust masses compared to non-obscured star-forming galaxies. We also analyzed the MIR colours of the Herschel-ATLAS sample against their specific star formation rates (SSFR), finding that galaxies with SSFRs below 0.1 Gyr$^{-1}$ display a steeper MIR spectral energy distribution (SED) slope than those with SSFRs above 0.1 Gyr$^{-1}$. This distinction suggests that galaxies with SSFRs below 0.1 Gyr$^{-1}$ are more heavily obscured by dust.

We investigate the extent to which large language models can replicate human moral judgments, specifically focusing on the tendency to grant exceptions to moral rules. Our study examines how well models can predict human judgments across various factors, including the severity of moral violations, the distinction between intentional and accidental actions, and specific exceptions to harm-based rules. Our results indicate that while models effectively replicate human judgments in many instances, they frequently fail to capture the nuanced nature of human exceptions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that models can be trained to better mirror human exceptional behavior by providing additional training data that explicitly includes these deviations. Finally, we introduce a novel methodology for analyzing the rationale behind human moral judgments, utilizing the models to generate explanations for specific decisions.
We demonstrate that any valuation ring which subsumes its residue field can be expressed as a directed limit of complete intersection rings.

This study examines the challenges of discretizing the Dirac equation in two dimensions, specifically addressing the problem of negative energy states. We demonstrate that the conventional staggered fermion approach yields a discretized Dirac operator featuring a large energy gap. This characteristic allows for straightforward application of standard numerical techniques, such as the Lanczos algorithm, to occupy only the lowest energy states. Furthermore, we investigate the continuum limit of the resulting energy spectrum and observe that the number of negative energy states remains constant, consistent with expectations from Lorentz symmetry.

This study introduces a novel communication-centric model for Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC) and platooning, designed to evaluate how communication failures affect vehicle dynamics. The proposed framework utilizes a Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy to govern longitudinal movements, with the objective of maintaining a constant inter-vehicle distance. The analysis specifically examines the consequences of intermittent data transmission, including latency and packet loss, on the stability of the entire platoon. Furthermore, the research investigates the influence of communication disruptions on the platoon's response to external disturbances.

The surge in social media usage has heightened the risk of misinformation spreading, prompting a need for robust verification mechanisms. This study introduces a new approach to assessing the credibility of Twitter users by integrating linguistic analysis with behavioral patterns. The proposed method employs a multi-stage pipeline: first, it utilizes a pre-trained language model to extract features from a user's tweet history; second, it applies a Random Forest classifier to determine trustworthiness. Validated against two distinct datasets, the model achieved an F1-score of 0.89 on the AIF21c dataset and 0.84 on the Enron dataset. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that the model's performance relies heavily on both linguistic cues and behavioral indicators.

The emergence of Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technology has enabled vehicles to exchange real-time data with infrastructure and other road users, thereby enhancing safety and efficiency. To support this, 5G networks have introduced Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) and Network Slicing, allowing MEC to manage network resources dynamically. This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a learn-as-you-go framework designed to create on-demand emergency slices for V2X environments. By leveraging MEC and network slicing, $\pi$-ROAD ensures that critical traffic data is transmitted with minimal latency. The framework utilizes a reinforcement learning agent to predict and allocate resources for these slices, while also determining the optimal placement of MEC servers. This approach is evaluated against two baseline methods: a static allocation strategy and a dynamic allocation strategy that only accounts for historical data. Simulation results demonstrate that $\pi$-ROAD outperforms both baselines, particularly in scenarios where the number of vehicles fluctuates unpredictably.

The rise of industrial automation has led to the emergence of collaborative robots (cobots) designed to work alongside humans, necessitating safety mechanisms that prevent injury during close interaction. This paper introduces CoHaptics, a collaborative framework that utilizes a forearm-mounted haptic interface to alert users of potential hazards. The system's efficacy was validated through experiments involving a robotic arm executing a pick-and-place task, where human participants manipulated a block within a confined workspace. Results indicate that CoHaptics significantly enhances operational safety, with the system demonstrating a 90% success rate in preventing collisions.

The rise of autonomous systems has sparked significant interest in the social, ethical, and legal dimensions of their integration into society. This paper examines the social and technical complexities of deploying autonomous vehicles within urban environments, arguing that these vehicles function as socio-technical systems. We propose a socio-technical framework for analyzing such systems, utilizing it to dissect the challenges associated with autonomous vehicle deployment. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this framework for regulatory policy and discuss its relevance to other autonomous systems, including drones and service robots.

This paper examines online caching within a framework where an online algorithm receives a probabilistic prediction regarding the likelihood of future requests. We introduce a novel online caching algorithm that leverages this prediction to achieve a competitive ratio of $\min\{2, 1 + \frac{1}{k-1} \sqrt{\frac{1-p}{p}}\}$, where $k$ represents the cache capacity and $p$ denotes the prediction accuracy. This proposed method significantly outperforms prior approaches, which are limited to a competitive ratio of $\min\{2, \frac{1}{k-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-p^2}}\}$, and comes with a runtime complexity of $O(k \log k)$. Furthermore, we establish a lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{p}})$ for the competitive ratio of any algorithm utilizing such probabilistic predictions. Consequently, our upper and lower bounds nearly converge, differing only by a logarithmic factor.

Attention mechanisms have proven highly effective in medical image segmentation, yet current methods often fail to leverage the complementary nature of different attention types. This study introduces a novel segmentation framework that integrates a bilateral attention mechanism with a novel trilateral component. The bilaterial module captures local image details, while the trilateral component synthesizes complementary information from the input, the output, and the intermediate feature maps. This design enables the network to focus on salient regions while filtering out irrelevant details. Furthermore, a real-time segmentation module is employed to generate immediate segmentation results. Experimental evaluations on three datasets—ACDC, Kvasir, and CVC-Capsule—demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/zhengxuan1996/TrilateralAttention.

This study introduces the linearized off-shell framework for four-dimensional 4+7 supergravity, which serves as the non-linearizable limit of the 11D supergravity action. The formalism is constructed using the 4+7 super-connection, a composite object comprising the 4D super-connection and the 7D super-connection. We establish the linearized Bianchi identities and demonstrate that, within the linearized off-shell regime, the 7D super-connection is fully determined by the 4D super-connection, thereby reducing the 7D Bianchi identities to zero. Furthermore, we derive the linearized on-shell 4+7 super-connection and confirm its compatibility with the 4D supersymmetry algebra.

The efficacy of machine learning models is heavily contingent upon the quality of their training data. This study introduces a novel approach to enhance data quality by leveraging the training dynamics inherent in Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs). We demonstrate that the progression of GBDT performance across boosting iterations offers valuable insights into the quality of individual training instances. Based on this observation, we developed a method to identify and filter out low-quality data points. Experimental results indicate that this approach yields substantial performance gains for GBDT models, with improvements reaching up to 10% in AUC scores.

The study examines the properties of the spin Hall effect within the integer quantum Hall regime, focusing on the spin Hall conductivity and its associated transport mechanisms. It is demonstrated that the spin Hall conductivity in this regime is quantized as an integer multiple of $e^2/h$, a result derived from the Berry curvature of the occupied Landau levels. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the spin Hall conductivity is governed by the spin splitting of Landau levels, which is modulated by the Zeeman effect. Consequently, the sign of the spin Hall conductivity is determined by the direction of this splitting. Additionally, the study investigates the transport characteristics of the spin Hall effect in the integer quantum Hall regime, specifically addressing the role of the Berry curvature in the spin Hall effect. Denoising pretraining of autoencoder-based language models has recently gained significant traction, yet its effectiveness is hindered by two primary challenges: the scarcity of high-quality pretraining data and the high computational cost of training. To address these issues, we introduce a new efficient denoising pretraining framework for large-scale autoencoding language models. Our approach leverages a straightforward yet effective noise augmentation strategy that utilizes model-generated signals to enhance data quality. Furthermore, we propose a new training objective designed to improve the model's ability to reconstruct the complete text sequence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art autoencoding language models across various benchmarks. Notably, we achieve a 1.5-fold reduction in training time while surpassing the performance of the current best model, which relies on the large-scale CodeBERT corpus.

Quantum networks are essential for advancing quantum information science and technology, yet accurately characterizing their topology remains a significant challenge. This work introduces a novel method for inferring the structure of quantum networks by utilizing local measurements. We demonstrate that, provided certain conditions are met, the network's topology can be deduced by examining the relationships among local observables and their corresponding eigenstates. Furthermore, we outline a practical protocol for enforces these conditions within actual quantum networks. Finally, the feasibility of this approach is validated through numerical simulations on a small-scale quantum network.

Information visualizations are a potent medium for presenting data, yet their effective use demands a deep understanding of design principles. This study investigates how novices comprehend these visualizations by analyzing crowd-sourced introductory explanations created by non-experts. We examined 100 such explanations across 10 distinct categories of introductory charts, uncovering that novices prioritize the identification of the visualization's type and the extraction of key insights. However, they frequently struggle to articulate the specific reasons for a visualization's efficacy or to explain how the data supports the conclusions drawn. Additionally, we identified that these introductions often omit critical data elements and fail to address the broader context of the information. Ultimately, these findings offer valuable guidance for both data literacy education and the design of more intuitive data visualizations.

We demonstrate that for any Hamiltonian $H$ with a ground state degeneracy, there exists a temperature $T^*$ such that the ground state of the system at $T=T^*$ coincides with the ground state at $T=0$. This phenomenon, termed the "maximum-entropy condensate," is illustrated using the transverse-field Ising model. Furthermore, we show that this condensate is generally not unique. We also discuss the connection between this concept and the link between the ground state and the thermodynamic limit.

Counterfactual reasoning is essential for human intelligence, enabling us to grasp cause-and-effect relationships, learn from mistakes, and make informed decisions. However, current approaches to counterfactuals often rely on assumptions that are either unrealistic or insufficient for practical applications. This paper introduces a new framework for counterfactual reasoning that addresses distributional ambiguity by leveraging the causal structure of the base factual scenario. This approach allows for the identification of which variables are necessary to adjust to ensure a counterfactual outcome remains valid despite uncertainty. We demonstrate the utility of this framework through two applications: first, in a medical context where it determines the specific variables required to evaluate the efficacy of a treatment; and second, in a robotics context where it enables robots to execute plans that are robust against distributional shifts.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of urban sound classification, covering the complete pipeline from data preprocessing to model training and evaluation. We introduce a new dataset derived from the Urban Sound Dataset (USD) by applying a rigorous cleaning process that ensures a balanced representation of sound categories. Additionally, we provide an in-depth comparison of various state-of-the-art models, including those based on transfer learning, to assess their performance. Our results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, attaining 0.86 F1-score and 0.85 classification accuracy on the test set.

We investigate supersymmetric AdS4 black holes within the framework of three-dimensional $\mathcal{N} \geq 3$ gauged supergravities coupled to matter fields. The analysis establishes that these black holes are uniquely determined by their mass, electric and magnetic charges, and angular momenta. The solution is constructed by applying a specific ansatz to the general form of supersymmetric vacua, which are characterized by a particular configuration of the scalar fields. The resulting solutions are presented in terms of the moduli fields and the parameters defining the black charges.

Focal-plane sensor-processors (FPSPs) are emerging as a promising alternative to conventional GPUs and FPGAs for deep learning inference. These devices integrate an image sensor and an on-chip processor to process images directly at the source, thereby reducing data movement and latency. However, their limited programmability and lack of software support currently restrict their deployment. This paper introduces Cain, a compiler designed to automatically generate code for FPSPs, targeting both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and standard convolutions. Cain streamlines the deployment of CNNs on FPSPs by automatically generating optimized assembly code and defining data movement strategies. The authors evaluate Cain on two distinct FPSP architectures: the Convolutional Neural Network Processor (CNN-PP) and the Convolutional Neural Network Processor (CNN-PP). Experimental results indicate that Cain achieves a speedup of 1.2x to 1.2x over existing approaches.

We investigate the constraints imposed by the Wess-Zumino term on the global symmetries within the effective field theory of Type IIB string backgrounds. Our analysis reveals that the relevant symmetry-breaking patterns are more intricate than anticipated, as axion decay factors can appear with fractional exponents. Furthermore, we demonstrate that generalized theta-terms can emerge in the effective action, even when absent from the underlying microscopic theory.

We introduce a new algorithm designed to learn Nash equilibria in stochastic games, utilizing regret-matching as its foundation. This approach is simulation-based, meaning it does not require access to the game's underlying model. We establish that the algorithm converges to a Nash equilibrium with a high probability, provided the game's structure is known. Our analysis demonstrates that, for two-player zero-sum games with a finite state space, the algorithm achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ represents the total number of actions taken. Furthermore, we examine scenarios where the game structure is unknown, showing that the method still converges to a Nash equilibrium with high probability, albeit with a convergence rate of $O(\log s / \sqrt{T})$, where $s$ denotes the cardinality of the state space.

This abstract presents a sound and complete calculus for Aristotle's modal syllogistic, denoted as $\mathcal{A}\mathcal{M}\mathcal{S}$, which interprets the system within a specific class of Kripke models. While the proof of soundness and completeness is not provided, the text outlines the proof theory of $\mathcal{A}\mathcal{M}\mathcal{S}$ and demonstrates how the results can be extended to establish the decidability of the system.

Quantum causal models serve as a vital instrument for investigating causal relationships within the quantum realm. This study examines the detection loophole inherent in quantum causal structure detection, which arises from the inability to definitively identify quantum causal structures when correlations are governed by the quantum-classical-classical (QCC) hybrid model. We demonstrate that a quantum detector can be engineered to distinguish between causal structures involving exclusively classical correlations and those containing quantum correlations. Furthermore, we introduce two countermeasures to mitigate the detection loophole: the first involves optimizing the detector's sensitivity to quantum correlations, while the second utilizes the quantum switch to generate quantum correlations from classical ones, thereby facilitating the identification of these correlations and the circumvention of the issue.

This paper introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning (RL) framework designed to optimize frame-level bit allocation for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) and H.265 streams. The proposed method aims to maximize the average Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of the entire video sequence by adjusting the quantization parameter (QP) for each frame. To achieve this, the RL agent utilizes a single policy network paired with two distinct value networks: one that estimates the immediate expected return and another that forecasts the long-term expected return. This dual-critic approach facilitates a more stable and efficient learning process. Experimental results indicate that the method outperforms existing RL-based solutions in terms of video quality.

The destruction of carbonaceous dust grains in protoplanetary disks is a pivotal process that governs the chemical evolution of these systems. This study examines the impact of carbon grain destruction on the final evolutionary stage of protoplanetary disks, characterized by the transition from a gas-rich to a gas-poor state. We demonstrate that the evaporation of carbon grains significantly elevates the abundance of carbon-bearing molecules in the gas phase, thereby altering the chemical composition of the disk. Specifically, we find that the destruction of carbon grains in the outer disk leads to a substantial increase in the abundance of CO gas, which in turn triggers the formation of CO$_2$ and H$_2$CO. Furthermore, we investigate the consequences of this gas-phase enrichment on the formation of complex organic molecules (COMs). Our results indicate that the evaporation of carbon grains in the outer disk causes a marked rise in the abundances of COMs such as methanol (CH$_3$OH) and methyl formate (H$_3$COO), thereby influencing the chemical pathways of the final disk evolution.

Cutting plane selection is a critical component of solving mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). While recent approaches have attempted to automate this task using machine learning, they often rely on heuristics that evaluate only the immediate local impact of a cut, neglecting its long-term consequences. This paper introduces a novel method for selecting cuts by employing a deep reinforcement learning agent trained to anticipate the future effects of those cuts. The agent learns to select cuts that maximize the reduction in the number of cuts required to solve a problem. Experimental results on standard benchmark MILP instances demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

We report on the superconducting properties of a Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$ single crystal, a Weyl semimetal featuring broken inversion symmetry. The material exhibits a superconducting transition temperature of $T_c = 2.5$ K. Analysis of the temperature dependence of the upper critical field $H_{c2}(T)$ reveals a downward curvature, which aligns with predictions from the two-fluid model. Furthermore, the temperature dependence of the London penetration depth $\lambda(T)$ follows a linear trend at low temperatures, suggesting that superconductivity arises from a spin-polarized Fermi surface.

This study introduces a novel method for automatically classifying bug reports using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. The approach employs a combination of Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) to generate feature vectors from the reports. These vectors are then processed by a Support Vector Machine (SVM) to determine the specific bug category. The system was evaluated on the 2012 dataset from the International Workshop on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ISMIS), which contains 1,000 bug reports from the Eclipse platform. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 84.5%, surpassing the 75.5% accuracy of the traditional baseline approach.

We investigate the electronic properties of anisotropic graphene, specifically examining how the coupling between sublattices varies with the angle of anisotropy. Our analysis reveals that this parameter significantly influences the nature of the system's phase transitions. Specifically, we observe that the transition from a semimetal to a ferromagnetic insulator is second-order, whereas the subsequent shift from a ferromagnetic insulator to a polarized state occurs via a first-order mechanism.

Named entity recognition (NER) has recently seen significant advancements through distantly-supervised approaches, which leverage the strengths of large-scale, weakly labeled text data to train teacher models that subsequently guide student models. However, these methods face two primary hurdles: first, the inherent noise within weak labels can degrade the performance of teacher models, and second, the resulting teacher model may lack the necessary domain expertise to effectively train student models. To address these issues, we introduce a new framework that integrates adaptive teacher learning with fine-grained student ensembles. The adaptive teacher learning component employs a dynamic strategy to identify and discard noisy training instances, thereby constructing a high-quality pseudo-label dataset. Concurrently, the fine-grained student ensemble mechanism utilizes a multi-task learning architecture to enhance the domain-specific capabilities of the final NER system. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CoNLL-2003 benchmark, with an F1 score of 89.5%.

The rise of social media has significantly transformed the tourism sector, with platforms like Twitter serving as a vital source of real-time data on traveler experiences. This study introduces a comprehensive framework for mining and analyzing such data, utilizing a case study of the city of Salzburg, Austria. We present a method to automatically categorize tweets into distinct experience types, such as accommodation, dining, and sightseeing. Furthermore, we demonstrate how to derive actionable insights from this data, including identifying the most popular experience categories, measuring sentiment, and mapping the geographic distribution of user-generated content.

This study introduces a data-driven framework for investigating the relationships between microstructure and properties in materials. The approach employs a data-driven surrogate model to approximate the solution of the underlying partial differential equations, utilizing a neural network with a physics-informed loss function. This method enforces adherence to the governing laws of physics, specifically the mechanical equilibrium condition, on the training data. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this technique by applying it to a representative material system: a polycrystalline single-phase aluminum alloy.

We report the detection of a companion to the 2 Myr-old CI Tau star, a member of the nearby T Tauri population. Using Gemini's NIRC2 instrument in the K'-band, we identified a source at a projected separation of 100 au with a contrast ratio of 10^-4. This object, designated CI Tau b, is located 1.5 arcseconds to the south-southeast of the primary. Its position angle of 160 degrees aligns with the CI Tau disk's orientation, and its orbital motion is consistent with a disk-influenced trajectory. CI Tau b's spectral energy distribution (SED) peaks in the near-infrared, indicating a spectral type of M6.5, with a mass estimate of 0.015 solar masses. This mass places CI Tau b in the planetary regime, making it the closest known M-type planet to its host star. We introduce a new potential capable of supporting off-center circular trajectories. By employing polar coordinates, we derive the corresponding radial potential and determine the angular momentum required for such orbits. Additionally, we calculate the angular momentum magnitude for a trajectory situated at the radius $r_0$ where the original potential reaches its minimum.

We establish a sharp Sobolev inequality for solutions of the equation $(-\Delta)^m u = u^{p-1}$ on a compact Riemannian manifold, where $m$ is a positive integer and $p$ is defined as $\frac{2m(n+2m-1)}{n}$. This result applies to manifolds with positive injectivity radius, provided the operator $(-\Delta)^m$ is defined via the geodesic distance. Our proof utilizes an integral representation of the solution, which is derived from the method of moving planes.

This paper introduces a new technique for estimating trajectories of multiple rigid objects in motion, utilizing a series of uncalibrated images. The proposed probabilistic framework employs a backward simulation method to estimate trajectories, which are then used to refine image models and generate updated image likelihoods. This iterative process continues until convergence. The method is tested on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its efficacy.

This paper introduces a new method for evaluating the stability of multi-infeed grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) that operate in the synchronous reference frame. The approach utilizes a specific model of the VSC that is represented as a constant current source in parallel with an admittance matrix. By applying the Nyquist criterion, the method determines the stability of the overall system. The paper also examines how the stability changes in relation to the VSC control parameters. Furthermore, the method's effectiveness is demonstrated through case studies on a two-infeed VSC system, with results validated against time-domain simulations.

This study introduces a novel approach to analyzing online signature characteristics, specifically targeting template complexity, distinctiveness, and repeatability. The methodology employs a multi-scale analysis of the spatial distribution of the signature's spatial trajectory, utilizing a scale-dependent metric known as the signature's fractal dimension. The proposed technique is validated through an experimental framework involving three distinct datasets comprising 1,000 signatures each. The results demonstrate that this metric effectively captures variations in writing style across these different collections.

We introduce a novel framework for designing persistent, contextualized data structures that operate atop an existing persistent linked list foundation. By utilizing this base, we establish a robust mechanism for managing contextual persistence and value propagation, enabling the construction of advanced structures such as hash maps, sets, and trees. Our analysis demonstrates that these structures retain the functional guarantees of their non-persistent equivalents, with the added capacity to persist historical states. Furthermore, we present an efficient algorithm for generating compact persistent, contextual trees that mirror the structural properties of standard treaps.

This study introduces an innovative approach for estimating human pose in 3D from video sequences. The method leverages a neural network architecture that integrates dilated convolutions with attention mechanisms to enhance pose estimation. The attention mechanism is designed to capture inter-frame dependencies, while dilated convolutions expand the receptive field to accommodate inter-joint dependencies. The system is trained on a dataset comprising 3D human poses derived from 2D poses and 3D camera parameters. Evaluation results demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy.

The Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZTI) instrument aboard the AstroSat mission serves as an X-ray and gamma-ray detector, primarily observing the CZTI's target fields. However, CZTI can also function as an X-ray all-sky monitor by analyzing occultations of bright celestial sources by the Earth. This study presents the first application of this technique using data from AstroSat, focusing on occultations of the Crab Nebula and the Cygnus X-1 binary system. We developed a specialized algorithm to reconstruct the full occultation profiles of these bright sources by combining observations from the narrow collimated field of view with the wide field of view of the Aditya-L1 satellite. This approach enables the reconstruction of the complete occultation profile for bright celestial sources, which can be used to study the structure of the interstellar medium and the source itself. We also discuss the advantages and limitations of this technique and its potential for future applications.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction in recent years, particularly for its capacity to facilitate secure, decentralized, and distributed data storage. This paper examines the asymptotic performance of a specific blockchain protocol, referred to as Blockchain-1, which is designed to manage the propagation of blocks across a network of nodes. We model the system as a network of $n$ nodes, where each node maintains a queue of blocks awaiting transmission. The objective is to determine the steady-state behavior of the block queue lengths as $n$ approaches infinity. To achieve this, we employ a fluid limit approach, where the discrete queue lengths are scaled by $n$ and analyzed in the limit as $n \to \infty$. The resulting limit process is characterized as a reflected Brownian motion, with the drift and diffusion coefficients derived from the underlying stochastic dynamics of the system. We demonstrate that the limit process possesses a stationary distribution, which is uniquely determined and fully characterized by the mean drift and diffusion parameters. Furthermore, we calculate the mean and variance of the stationary distribution, which are expressed in terms of the drift and diffusion coefficients. Finally, we discuss the practical implications of these findings for the design and analysis of blockchain protocols.

This study investigates the mass spectra of doubly heavy tetraquarks, defined as $QQ\bar{q}\bar{q}'$ (where $Q$ represents a charm or bottom quark and $q, q'$ are light quarks), utilizing an improved chromomagnetic interaction (CMI) model. The C$_{MI}$ incorporates a linear confining potential and accounts for the mixing between color antitriplet and sextet configurations. By applying the C$_{MI}$ model to the $SU(3)$ flavor-symmetric sector, we calculate the mass spectra for $BB\bar{u}\bar{u}$, $BB\bar{u}\bar{d}$, $BB\bar{d}\bar{d}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $BB\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $

We investigate the impact of electroweak vacuum metastability on the gauge hierarchy problem. Specifically, we examine scenarios where the Higgs potential, characterized by a negative minimum, becomes unstable at a scale significantly lower than the Planck scale. Our findings indicate that under these conditions, the hierarchy problem can be resolved even with a top quark mass situated near the critical boundary of metastability.

This paper demonstrates the q-logarithmic Sobolev inequality through a combination of heat flow analysis and a rearrangement technique, while also establishing a q-logarithmic Sobolev inequality alongside a p-Talagrand inequality using Carnot-Caratheodory balls.

This study examines the Minimum Discrepancy Inference (MDI) method, a Bayesian framework that derives a posterior distribution from a prior and a likelihood. The likelihood is constructed by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the data distribution and the model distribution. The KL divergence is a specific instance of Bregman divergence; consequently, the MDI method is generalized to accommodate any Bregman divergence. The authors demonstrate that the resulting posterior distribution is uniquely determined and that the KL divergence between the data distribution and the resulting MDI posterior is minimized. Furthermore, the paper establishes that the MDI posterior is the Bregman divergence projection of the prior onto the model space. Additionally, the study reveals that the MDI posterior is a member of the exponential family whenever the prior is, and it is shown that the MDI method is equivalent to the Maximum Entropy (ME) method. The paper also proves that the ME problem can be formulated as a linear programming task.

We introduce wildNeRF, a method designed to generate view synthesis for dynamic, in-the-wild scenes using sparse monocular inputs. This approach employs a neural radiance field (NeRF) to model both geometry and appearance, incorporating a differentiable renderer to optimize for multi-view consistency. To ensure robustness against sparse and noisy observations, we utilize a differentiable warping module to leverage information from neighboring frames. Additionally, we develop a novel regularizer to mitigate the severe overfitting issues common in NeRF training with sparse data. Our results demonstrate that wildNeRf achieves superior performance compared to existing NeRF variants, producing high-quality novel view synthesis for dynamic scenes with minimal input data.

We examine the distribution of lengths of the longest primitive periodic orbits found within a collection of random, edge-transitive quantum graphs, where each graph consists of $N$ edges. By defining the distribution of the longest length $L_N$ through the cumulative function $P_N(x) = \text{Prob}(L_N \leq x)$, we derive an exact analytical expression for its first moment, $\langle L_N \rangle$. This calculation relies on the mean density of periodic orbits and the total periodic orbit count, both of which are determined using combinatorial methods. Furthermore, we provide a numerical analysis of the results, which reveals that the asymptotic behavior of $\langle L_N \rangle$ follows a linear trend with a slope of $1.5$ as $N$ increases.

This study introduces a novel technique for determining the periods of periodic variable stars. The method involves plotting the light curve against a reference curve that shares the same period and shape, then calculating the correlation coefficient between them. By analyzing how this coefficient varies with different periods, one can identify the correct period as the value corresponding to the peak coefficient. The method's effectiveness was validated using the well-known Cepheid variables, $\delta$ Cep and W Virginis stars, $\delta$ Vir, alongside the RR Lyrae star, $\delta$ Sct. The resulting periods align well with established values, and the approach is particularly advantageous for its simplicity and speed, making it ideal for processing large datasets.

This study addresses the challenge of locating the nearest system characterized by negative imaginary (NI) properties to a specified, typically unstable system that lacks such properties. By utilizing a novel class of system transformations, the authors develop a streamlined algorithm that efficiently identifies the closest NI system. This method proves effective for diverse scenarios, including optimal controller synthesis for systems with negative imaginary characteristics. Additionally, the paper explores an extension of this approach to determine the closest NI system within a specific framework of affine parameterization.

This paper introduces a continual learning approach designed to train monolingual end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems in a continuous manner. The primary objective is to enable the training of an ASR model on a new language without compromising the performance of previously acquired languages. The study evaluates continual learning within the context of End-to-End Conformer-Transducer (EER-T) architectures, utilizing a combination of Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) and knowledge distillation. Experimental results indicate that this proposed method effectively prevents catastrophic forgetting, thereby sustaining high performance across all previously learned languages while successfully acquiring new ones.

Code-switching, the practice of alternating between two or more languages within a single conversation, is a prevalent linguistic phenomenon. This paper details the NLP-CIC team's approach to the Sentiment Analysis sub-task of the 2020 ICMLC evaluation, utilizing a straightforward deep learning model. The study highlights key challenges specific to code-switching, such as the scarcity of training data and the presence of noisy labels, and outlines strategies to mitigate these issues. Furthermore, it examines the impact of various preprocessing techniques and presents an analysis of the resulting sentiment predictions.

This study explores a minimal three-loop radiative seesaw framework that simultaneously accounts for the origin of matter-antimatter asymmetry and the nature of dark matter. The model incorporates a sterile neutrino, a sterile charged lepton, a sterile scalar, and a fermionic dark matter candidate. We demonstrate that the intricate dark matter relic density can be precisely reproduced by adjusting the annihilation cross-section through a resonant mechanism. Furthermore, we analyze the model's phenomenology, specifically its predictions for sterile neutrino production in the early universe and the resulting sterile neutrino mass scale, as well as the potential detection signatures of dark matter in direct detection experiments.

Predicting user responses in online settings is a critical challenge for building effective recommendation systems. While recent neural network approaches have demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional methods, they often struggle to explicitly model complex user-item interactions due to their inability to capture higher-order interactions. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel product-based neural network architecture designed to explicitly model these interactions. Our approach leverages a user's historical item sequence and an input item to predict the likelihood of a future click. We achieve this by utilizing an attentive mechanism to weigh the relevance of past items and employing a tensor product layer to synthesize their joint effects. Comprehensive experiments on a large-scale industrial dataset reveal that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, validating its effectiveness.

This study introduces a robust active and passive beamforming design for Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) within Cell-Free networks, accounting for potential hardware imperfections in both the access points (APs) and the IRS. Specifically, we address the challenge of maximizing the minimum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) across all APs, subject to constraints on AP transmit power, IRS reflection coefficients, and hardware error bounds. To achieve this, we formulate the problem as a non-convex optimization task and develop a low-complexity, suboptimal solution using the successive convex approximation (SCA) method. This approach iteratively refines the solution by transforming the non-convex constraints into convex surrogates. Furthermore, we extend the proposed framework to a distributed architecture, where APs jointly optimize their active beamforming vectors and exchange information with a central controller to optimize IRS passive beamforming. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed robust active and passive beamforming strategies significantly outperform existing benchmark schemes.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern CPU architectures, and Dynamic Branch Prediction (DBP) has emerged as a promising avenue to enhance branch prediction accuracy by leveraging machine learning. This survey paper examines recent DBP research, focusing on the methodologies and architectures of various deep learning models. We also discuss evaluation methodologies and provide a comparative analysis of different approaches. Furthermore, we identify unresolved challenges and outline potential future research directions within the field of dynamic branch prediction.

This paper introduces an imitation learning framework for active camera control within object tracking systems. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to identify the optimal camera angle for capturing the target object. By training the CNN on a dataset of image pairs, it learns to map the target's position and orientation to the ideal viewing angle. This approach was implemented and tested on a robotic cart equipped with a camera, where the controller determines the next angle based on the current image analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that the tracking system successfully maintains the target even when starting from suboptimal camera perspectives.

This paper investigates the second-order, non-linear difference equation defined by $x_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha x_{n}^2 + \beta x_{n} + \gamma}{\beta x_{n} + \alpha}$. This equation arises from a spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Ising model featuring a nearest-neighbor interaction and an external magnetic field, specifically within the context of partition functions for the Solid-On-Solid (SOS) model. We analyze the equation's roots and demonstrate that, for certain parameter values, the associated SOS model possesses multiple Gibbs measures.

Entangled photon resonance energy transfer (ERET) is a process where one entangled photon in a pair is absorbed by an atom, while its partner induces a quantum transition in a second atom without being absorbed. This study demonstrates that, unlike traditional resonance energy transfer (RET), entangled photon ERET (ERET) remains viable even within lossy environments. We further show that ERET can be effectively controlled by adjusting the spatial separation between the two target atoms.

This study calculates the strong coupling constants for charmed and bottom mesons interacting with light vector mesons using QCD sum rules. The analysis incorporates the contributions of four-point condensates, the Borel parameter, and the convergence of the OPE, while also examining the reliability of the sum rule results. The findings indicate that the strong coupling constants for $D$ and $D^*$ mesons coupled to light vector mesons are of comparable magnitude, as are those for $D^*_s$ mesons. Furthermore, the strong coupling constants for $D$ and $D^*_s$ mesons coupled to light vector mesons are found to be similar. Regarding bottom mesons, the strong coupling constant for coupling to a light vector meson is approximately 1.5 times larger than that for charmed mesons. Finally, the strong coupling constants for coupling a $B$ meson to a light vector meson are roughly comparable to those for coupling a $B^*$ meson to a light vector meson.
This document outlines the anticipated upcoming neutrino experiments, summarizing their projected designs, physics objectives, and potential outcomes.

This paper examines the linear regression estimator of average treatment effects, incorporating both continuous and binary outcomes, while accounting for multiple covariates. We establish that this estimator is equivalent to weighted least squares, where the weights are determined by a linear function of covariates and do not necessarily reflect the true importance of each sample in causal inference. We demonstrate that the linear regression estimator can be decomposed into two components: the weighted least squares estimator and a residual term. We further analyze the asymptotic properties of both formulations and prove that the residual term is asymptotically linear, thereby enabling the application of standard statistical tools to both estimators. Additionally, we provide illustrative examples showing that finite sample bias in the linear regression estimator may be substantial, even when the propensity score is nearly constant.

This paper introduces a novel, model-free wide-area damping control strategy for voltage source converters (VSCs) that leverages phasor measurement units (PMUs). The approach employs a simple low-pass filter to extract the oscillatory components of local measurements, which are then converted into corrective signals for active and reactive power. The proposed method's effectiveness is validated through a case study on a modified IEEE 118-bus system, demonstrating its ability to enhance inter-area damping. The results indicate that the scheme significantly outperforms conventional droop control, especially in heavily damped oscillatory modes.

We investigate the collective dynamics of two atoms coupled to a single-mode optical cavity, focusing on their collective decay and dissipation processes. By employing a quantum master equation, we analyze the system's collective behavior and identify a steady-state subradiant state. This state is achieved by balancing the collective decay and dissipation rates, a balance that can be tuned via the cavity detuning parameter. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the collective decay mechanism can be switched on or off, allowing for the creation of entanglement between the two atoms.

This paper examines the asymptotic stability of a kink within the sine-Gordon framework subjected to time-dependent perturbations. We demonstrate that when the perturbation period is sufficiently large, the kink remains stable even under odd symmetries, provided it is subject to internal modes. However, this stability is contingent upon the kink's initial position, a condition that varies depending on the specific period of the perturbation.

The J-PARC facility in Japan is set to commence operations in 2009, with a primary aim of investigating the internal structure of hadrons. This paper outlines the J-PARC program's objectives and highlights its potential contributions to research on the color transparency effect.

Consistency training is a powerful, model-agnostic method for enhancing the generalization capabilities of various machine learning models. This paper introduces Consistency Training with Virtual Adversarial Discrete Perturbation (CVDPD), an approach that extends consistency training to handle discrete data. The method involves generating discrete perturbations from the original input and enforcing that the model's predictions remain consistent despite these changes. To address the challenge of defining meaningful perturbations for discrete data, CVDPD utilizes the concept of virtual adversarial direction. This involves identifying a virtual adversarial sample in the continuous domain and converting it into a discrete format to serve as the perturbation. Empirical evaluations on multiple discrete datasets demonstrate that CVDPD significantly improves consistency training performance.

This paper introduces a new multi-frame collaborative approach designed to enhance the detection of polyps in endoscopic videos. The method leverages the inherent temporal coherence of these videos to boost detection accuracy. Specifically, we propose a new multi-frame collaborative module that integrates information from multiple frames into a single frame. This module employs a spatial-temporal feature transformation mechanism, which aligns and fuses features across different frames to create a unified representation. This strategy effectively captures both the spatial and temporal characteristics of polyps, thereby improving overall detection performance. Experiments conducted on the Kvasir-SEG dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The paper introduces a new technique for sampling from streams, which generates a probabilistic, unequal sample where each element's selection likelihood depends exclusively on its arrival order. This approach is inherently probabilistic, meaning the resulting sample composition varies across different realizations of the same stream. The authors demonstrate that the method is both versatile and straightforward to implement. Furthermore, they establish the method's theoretical soundness by proving the probability of selecting any specific subset of size $k$ adheres to a closed-form expression.

The $rp$-process, a rapid proton capture sequence occurring in the most proton-rich nuclei, is pivotal for synthesizing elements in the mass range of 20 to 60. A critical aspect of this process involves the $^{56}$Ni waiting point, where the reaction flow pauses due to the relatively slow $\beta$-decay of $^{56}$Ni. This study presents the first experimental measurement of the $^{56}$Ni decay rate and demonstrates that the decay emits a proton with a delay time of 0.001 seconds. This newly identified $\beta$-delayed proton emission bypasses the traditional waiting point, enabling the rapid synthesis of elements up to $^{57}$Zn. These findings are essential for refining models of $rp$-process nucleosynthesis.

We establish the finiteness of torsion points found in a specific orbit under an arithmetic pencil's action. This outcome serves as an arithmetic counterpart to the classical Manin-Mumford theorem regarding torsion points on curves of genus at least 2. Our approach relies on the ergodicity of such arithmetic pencils, a property that parallels the dynamics of ergodic actions by semisimple groups on quotient spaces of Lie groups by compact subgroups.

This study reports on the search for very high-energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from 14 pulsars located in the Northern sky, which were previously identified as potential candidates by the HESS collaboration. The analysis utilized data from the VERITAS instrument, a ground-based Cherenkov telescope array situated in the southwestern United States. The observations span a total exposure of 10.3 hours, with observations conducted between 2008 and 2013. The study employed a likelihood-based method to search for VHE gamma-ray emission, with a focus on the pulsars' surrounding regions. The results show no significant evidence of gamma-ray emission from these pulsars, with upper limits on the fluxes set at the 95% confidence level. The fluxes were then compared to the expected fluxes from the pulsars' magnetospheres and wind regions, with the results showing that the fluxes are consistent with the expected fluxes from these regions. This study examines a reaction-diffusion equation characterized by nonlocal boundary conditions within an open set exhibiting a fractal boundary. We establish the existence of a global attractor and determine its fractal dimension. Furthermore, we derive a regularity property for the system's solution.

We introduce a machine learning (ML) approach designed to identify extragalactic ultra-compact dwarfs (UCDs) and globular clusters (GCs) in the COSMOS2015 dataset. This dataset comprises 1.4 terabytes of multi-wavelength imaging data from 2.2 billion galaxies, covering 2.5 square degrees. Our method utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to detect UCDs and GCs, achieving a 90% detection rate with a 90% purity. To enhance interpretability, we employ an explainable AI technique known as Grad-CAM, which visualizes the model's decision-making process by highlighting specific image regions. These visualizations reveal that the model primarily relies on the morphology of the objects and their surrounding environments for classification. Furthermore, we apply the model to the COSMOS2015 catalog to generate a new catalog of extragalactic UCDs and GCs.

Simulations are a fundamental element of the scientific method, enabling researchers to test hypotheses and evaluate the performance of algorithms and systems. Despite their widespread use across various domains, simulations remain underutilized within recommender systems. This paper examines the current state of simulation in this field, identifies its primary challenges, and highlights opportunities for future research. We argue that integrating simulations into recommender systems research can significantly advance the field, particularly by addressing the critical issue of evaluating online A/B tests.

This study examines the asymptotic behavior of the truncated sample mean when applied to independent and identically distributed random variables with an infinite mean, specifically under a regular variation condition with index $-1 < \alpha < 0$. We establish that the truncated sample mean converges in probability to a deterministic constant. Furthermore, we derive a precise asymptotic distribution for the fluctuations around this limit, which is characterized as a non-Gaussian, totally skewed distribution belonging to the domain of attraction of a stable law. These findings are then applied to construct a rigorous asymptotic framework for large-sample hypothesis testing concerning the truncated sample mean in the context of extremely heavy-tailed distributions.

Motor Imagery (MI) Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) systems offer significant potential for assisting individuals with severe motor impairments. However, the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of EEG signals and the high dimensionality of the data present substantial challenges for MI-BCI applications. This study introduces a new Sinc-based Convolutional Neural Network (SCNN) architecture designed to address these issues. The SCNN framework integrates Sinc kernels into the convolutional layers to enhance the network's ability to extract features from EEG data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SCNN achieves superior performance compared to standard CNNs and other established BCI methods. Furthermore, the research indicates that the SCNN's efficacy is highly dependent on the bandwidth of the Sinc kernels.

We examine the $AdS_2$ analogue of the correspondence principle, which posits that the $AdS_2$ isometry algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be recovered from a noncommutative $AdS_2$ spacetime by quantizing the coordinate algebra. This framework extends the concept of the correspondence principle to noncommutative $AdS_2$ theories, where the quantized coordinate algebra is identified with the Virasoro algebra. We demonstrate that this extended principle holds for noncommutative $AdS_2$ spacetimes constructed via the Moyal product.

Kidney transplant recipients often face a shortage of compatible organs, leading many to accept incompatible kidneys paired with post-transplant desensitization protocols. This study introduces a novel framework to determine the optimal acceptance rate for incompatible kidneys, balancing the benefits of expanded acceptance against the risks of elevated rejection. By modeling the joint evolution of a recipient's health and the kidney's age, we define an optimal stopping criterion for assessing rejection probability. Using this model, we calculate the optimal acceptance threshold and evaluate how varying this rate influences both the number of transplants and overall recipient health.

This study introduces a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Hidden Markov Model (HMM) framework designed to enhance the predictive performance of both components. The proposed method leverages the LSTM's capacity to model complex, non-linear dynamics by generating hidden states that are subsequently processed by an HMM to capture the underlying system's linear structure. This integration allows the combined model to effectively handle both linear and non-linear characteristics. The efficacy of the approach is validated through its application to the Mackey-Glass time series, where it demonstrates superior results compared to standalone LSTM and HMM models.

This study examines the boundedness and compactness properties of generalized Volterra integral operators acting on weighted Bergman spaces within the unit disk. Furthermore, the work establishes a boundedness and compactness criterion for generalized Toeplitz operators on these spaces, with a specific focus on the case involving the unit circle's weighted Bergman spaces.

Cross-lingual multi-task models (CLMMs) are designed to handle multiple tasks across various languages, and this paper presents a method for efficiently compressing them. We achieve compression by utilizing a shared language-specific encoder and a shared task-agnostic representation. Our approach involves training a language-specific encoder for each supported language, followed by a multi-task learning stage that fine-tunes these encoders using a shared representation. We evaluate our method on two language-agnostic tasks: language-agnostic named entity recognition (NER) and language-agnostic part-of-speech (POS) tagging. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces model size by 60% while maintaining performance comparable to the state-of-the-art.

Open data represents a rapidly expanding field that has garnered significant attention from both industry and academia. This article offers a personal viewpoint on the current state of open data research, highlighting the challenges and opportunities it presents. It examines the obstacles involved in releasing data, particularly within the healthcare sector, and proposes a potential solution.

This paper examines decomposed Richelot isogenies applied to the Jacobians of hyperelliptic curves. We present an explicit construction for such isogenies using generalized Howe curves, which serve as a higher-genus analogue to standard Howe curves. Additionally, we offer a concrete formula for these isogenies in cases where the domain Jacobian is that of a hyperelliptic curve, and we provide a specific example of a decomposed Richelot isogenity involving the Jacobian of a decomposed hyperelliptic curve of genus 5.

We report the discovery of three magnetic hot subdwarf stars, designated SDSS J122222+000000, SDSS J122222+000000, and SDSS J122222+000000, utilizing data from the SDSS and the HST. These stars exhibit strong Zeeman signatures in their spectra, indicating the presence of magnetic fields. By analyzing their spectral lines and photometry, we determined their fundamental parameters, including effective temperatures, surface gravities, and radii. Furthermore, we performed a detailed analysis of the Zeeman signatures to derive the magnetic field strengths and map their geometry. Our results suggest that these stars likely formed via a merger event, which could have triggered the generation of their magnetic fields. Additionally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the evolution of hot subdwarf stars and the population of magnetic white dwarfs.

This work introduces an algorithm for computing the truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) of positive semi-definite (PSD) matrices. The approach leverages a decomposition of the PSD matrix into a sum of random, low-rank PSD components, followed by the application of volume sampling to each term. We establish that this method achieves a failure probability of at most $\delta$ while incurring a computational cost of $\tilde{O}(r^2 \cdot \text{nnz}(A) \cdot \text{poly}(k, \delta^{-1}))$, where $A$ is the PSD matrix, $r$ denotes the rank, and $k$ represents the number of retained singular vectors. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this algorithm can be adapted to handle general symmetric matrices.

This paper presents WikiHist.html, a complete English Wikipedia dataset comprising every revision version of all articles in a single HTML format. The dataset includes all articles and their histories, even those lacking a current version, and is freely available for download. We describe the dataset's structure, its creation process, and its utility for research. Additionally, we provide several examples of its application in various fields of study.

We introduce a new class of magnetic textures in twisted bilayer systems, specifically polar meron-antimeron networks, which emerge from the interplay between the moir\'e potential and interlayer spin coupling. These structures consist of meron and antimeron pairs aligned along the direction of the moir\'e lattice vectors. The formation of these polar configurations is driven by the specific topological nature of merons and antimerons, which possess half-integer winding numbers, combined with the spatial symmetry of the moir\'e lattice. We demonstrate that these polar networks can be stabilized by applying an external electric field perpendicular to the plane of the system. Furthermore, we explore the potential applications of these networks in spintronics, particularly regarding their ability to generate polar skyrmions and to serve as a mechanism for manipulating magnetic textures through electric fields.

This paper introduces a novel framework for analyzing the dynamics of a universe with a non-trivial topology, specifically one that is a 3-torus. We establish a new set of variables and corresponding equations of motion that are mathematically equivalent to the standard Friedmann equations derived from general relativity. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding wave function for a 3-torus universe and a set of uncertainty principles governing these non-trivial spatial conditions.

We present a comprehensive experimental and theoretical study of the motion of spherical colloids within nematic liquid crystals confined by wavy walls. Our findings indicate that colloids exhibit a periodic trajectory, oscillating between the wall peaks and valleys. This dynamic is driven by the interplay between the colloids' attraction toward the wall and the elastic forces within the liquid crystal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the colloidal path can be modulated by adjusting the wall amplitude and the ratio of the colloid size to the wall wavelength. Additionally, we observe a transition from periodic motion to chaotic behavior as the wall wavelength decreases. These results offer valuable insights into the design of tunable colloidal transport systems and provide a framework for understanding the dynamics of soft particles in complex fluid environments.

This study examines how asteroid shape affects the stability of surface boulders during a planet's flyby. We demonstrate that the asteroid's shape plays a critical role in determining whether a surface boulder remains stable or becomes unstable during such an event. Specifically, for a fixed planet-asteroid distance, increasing the aspect ratio of the asteroid (making it more elongated) raises the critical size required for a boulder to remain stable. This finding suggests that asteroids with highly elongated shapes possess a greater surface sensitivity to close planetary passages, allowing smaller boulders to remain in place compared to more spherical bodies.

Molecular dynamics simulations are essential for investigating the dynamics of biomolecules, yet they face significant challenges in efficiently sampling rare events. This study introduces a quantum algorithm designed to overcome these limitations by utilizing quantum superposition to concurrently explore multiple states. We demonstrate that this approach can calculate the free energy landscape of a system with an exponential reduction in computational complexity compared to classical methods. Furthermore, we outline a practical implementation of this algorithm on current quantum hardware and validate its efficacy through numerical simulations of a protein folding process.

We introduce MAPPIES, a novel Monte Carlo tool designed to simulate the scattering of photons via the inverse Compton process. This code is specifically tailored for modeling radiation emitted by relativistic electrons within astrophysical environments, particularly those involving partially polarized photon fields. The simulation tracks the evolution of photon polarization states throughout the scattering process, enabling the calculation of the resulting polarization in the emitted radiation. This capability is essential for interpreting observations of polarized emission from sources such as blazars and gamma-ray bursts. The paper details the implementation of the software and presents initial findings regarding the polarization characteristics of photons scattered off a partially polarized, isotropic, and monochromatic photon field.

The Arctic Ocean's sea ice thickness distribution (SITD) is a critical indicator of the region's cryosphere state, yet its seasonal dynamics remain poorly understood. This study utilizes the Community Earth System Model (CESM) to investigate the seasonal evolution of SITD, specifically examining the impacts of sea ice dynamics and thermodynamics. Results indicate that the model accurately reproduces the annual cycle of Arctic SITD, with sea ice dynamics playing a more significant role in the autumn and winter months. Furthermore, the research highlights that the model's representation of SITD is highly sensitive to the parameterization of first-year ice thermodynamics.

We investigate the Weierstrass semigroup $H_{\mathbf{\infty}}$ at multiple points on specific maximal curves that possess a unique structure, distinguishing them from cases where the cover is the Hermitian curve.

Singing Voice Synthesis (SVS) represents a specialized subfield of speech synthesis that generates human-like audio by combining lyrics with melodic and rhythmic data. While traditional SVS methods relied on intricate, hand-crafted models, the advent of deep learning has recently enabled the creation of systems capable of producing high-fidelity audio. This survey offers a comprehensive review of the latest deep learning-driven SVS architectures, examining their underlying principles, specific methodologies, and performance outcomes. Furthermore, the text addresses key evaluation metrics and standard benchmark datasets used to assess SVS systems. The paper concludes by identifying current limitations and outlining prospective research avenues for future development in this domain.
