Hyperspectral spectral super-resolution (HSSR) involves reconstructing high-dimensional spectral data from low-dimensional inputs. While deep learning has emerged as a potent tool for this task, existing deep neural network (DNN) approaches often fail to adequately capture the inherent sparsity of high-dimensional spectra. To address this, we introduce the Pixel-aware Deep Function-mixture Network (PFM-Net), which models high-dimensional spectral data as a mixture of low-dimensional components. This approach offers two key advantages: first, it explicitly incorporates the sparsity of high-dimensional spectra; second, it learns the mapping between high-dimensional spectral components and their corresponding low-dimensional counterparts. The PFM-Net framework consists of three primary modules: a pixel-aware spectral decoder, a pixel-aware spectral encoder, and a high-dimensional spectral estimator. The decoder and encoder are designed to learn the spatial distribution of spectral components, while the estimator predicts the mapping between these components. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PFM-Net outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in HSSR tasks.

This study introduces a geotagging framework that integrates contextual awareness to identify the precise locations of objects within an image. The proposed method employs a two-stage process: first, it determines the most probable location for a specific object by leveraging contextual clues, and second, it refines this estimate to pinpoint the exact coordinates. The location estimation stage utilizes a context-aware model that synthesizes object features with scene context, while the coordinate refinement stage utilizes a model that estimates the object's spatial relationship to its surroundings. The framework was tested on a dataset comprising 1,000 images of landmarks and their associated tags. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art geotagging methods.

Dam reservoirs are essential for water management, flood control, and energy production, yet monitoring their capacity is critical for ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of these structures. This study introduces a novel approach to automatically detect dam reservoirs in satellite images by leveraging a specialized metric learning framework. The method utilizes a deep neural network to generate feature embeddings, which are then optimized using a tailored loss function designed to maximize the separation between positive and negative examples. To address the significant class imbalance inherent in remote sensing data, we employ a metric learning strategy that dynamically adjusts the weighting of positive and negative samples. Furthermore, we develop a new data augmentation technique that generates additional training samples by applying random transformations to existing images. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in both accuracy and robustness.

Quasi-compact quasi-separated (QFS) spaces represent a broad generalization of Noetherian spaces. This QFS class encompasses numerous non-Noetherian topological structures, including specific non-Noetherian schemes, while retaining many Noetherian properties. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the QFS concept, detailing its defining characteristics and established results.

We introduce a new approach to pinpointing the type of point-of-interest (POI) by leveraging user-generated content from social media. This task involves categorizing a POI into a specific type based on user reviews and shared images. Our method employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract features from images, while utilizing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to process review text. These extracted features are then integrated into a fully connected neural network to determine the POI type. To validate our model's effectiveness, we conducted experiments on a real-world dataset. The results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study investigates the relationship between earnings call content and subsequent stock price movements. We introduce a novel method for extracting content from these calls, which involves converting transcripts into a structured representation of the conversation. This approach enables the analysis of specific topics discussed and the interactions between speakers. Our findings indicate that the order of topics addressed during the call and the engagement patterns between management and analysts are significant predictors of future stock performance.

This study addresses the deployment of sensors within homogeneous and heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (WSNs) characterized by restricted communication ranges. In homogeneous WSNs, every sensor shares identical sensing and communication capabilities. Conversely, heterogeneous networks consist of sensors with varying sensing and communication attributes. The objective is to determine the minimum quantity of sensors required to achieve full coverage of a target area, ensuring every point is monitored by at least one sensor. The analysis examines both one-dimensional and two-dimensional scenarios, with the latter assuming a circular sensing field.

We introduce a quantum eigenstate filtering protocol that leverages polynomial approximation to extract specific selected eigenstates from an arbitrary unitary evolution operator. This approach is benchmarked against the conventional method, which relies on quantum signal processing. Our technique achieves a quadratic improvement in complexity regarding the targeted eigenvalue, while maintaining dependence on the spectral norm of the input operator that is identical to the standard approach. We demonstrate the utility of this algorithm by applying it to the Hamiltonian simulation problem and the task of solving linear systems of equations.

We examine the static, self-dual compact gauged baby skyrmion within a nonlinear medium, focusing on the influence of the background gauge field on its structure. This study analyzes the skyrmion's energy and magnetization, alongside its topological charge, to determine how these properties vary with background gauge flux. Furthermore, the paper explores the creation of background vortices and the emergence of monopoles linked to singularities in the skyrmion's topological density.

The Standard Model (SM) has been rigorously tested and validated through numerous experiments, yet it is not considered the final theory of nature. Numerous experiments have already placed stringent limits on potential interactions beyond the SM, and the search for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) remains a primary focus of the current particle physics program. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent and upcoming searches for new interactions, covering both lepton and hadron colliders. We examine the implications of SMEFT (Standard Model Effective Field Theory) for BSM phenomena and outline the potential reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and the Future Circular Collider (FCC) in probing these new interactions.

Whole-cell computational models represent the most comprehensive depictions of cellular systems available to date. These models are constructed by integrating vast quantities of experimental data, encompassing both the structural and functional dynamics of cells. The resulting models are complex, necessitating the use of advanced computational tools and methodologies. This review outlines the current state of whole-cell modeling, highlighting key challenges and potential future trajectories.

This paper introduces a novel mobile multi-view object image search framework designed to enhance the accuracy of image-based object retrieval. The system utilizes a mobile device to capture multiple perspectives of a target object, which are then processed to generate a unified 3D representation. This representation is subsequently matched against a database of 3D models to identify the most similar candidates. We propose a new method for constructing a unified 3D model capable of accommodating objects with varying geometries and textures. Furthermore, we develop a novel similarity metric that effectively integrates both 2D visual features and 3D structural data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Epileptic seizure detection is a critical endeavor aimed at enhancing the quality of life for individuals with epilepsy. While numerous machine learning methods have been developed for this purpose, they often struggle with high computational demands, making them unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper introduces an in-depth analysis of Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) strategies designed to optimize learning processes for seizure detection. The study evaluates three distinct HDC approaches: (1) a standard baseline utilizing conventional vector-based methods, (2) a memory-based model leveraging temporal data, and (3) a hybrid model combining both vector and memory-based techniques. Experimental results indicate that the hybrid model outperforms the other two approaches, achieving a 99.99% accuracy rate in identifying seizures. Furthermore, the hybrid model demonstrates superior efficiency by reducing computational complexity by 50% compared to the baseline.

This study examines the cosmological implications of gravitational waves (GWs) as standard sirens, specifically focusing on the Hubble constant ($H_0$) using GWs from binary black holes (BBHs) detected by the Deci-hertz Observatory (DHO). We employ a Bayesian framework to derive the posterior distribution of $H_0$ based on the GW luminosity distance ($D_L$) and the redshift of host galaxies. Our analysis indicates that a BBH catalog of 100 events with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exceeding 10 would yield a $1\sigma$ uncertainty of $1.1\%$ on $H_0$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the GW luminosity distance can be constrained to a $1\sigma$ precision of $1.1\%$ by combining the GW signal with the redshift from the host galaxy and the redshift of the nearest galaxy within the same cluster. We also investigate the impact of including additional BBH events with an SNR between 5 and 10, finding that such an inclusion reduces the $1\sigma$ uncertainty on $H_0$ to $0.8\%$. Finally, we discuss the potential of future space-based GW detectors to improve the precision of the Hubble constant measurement.

This paper introduces a new multilingual dataset for question answering over DBpedia and Wikidata, covering nine languages: Czech, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, and Spanish. The dataset consists of 1,000 questions per language, totaling 9,000 questions, each with five manually annotated answers verified by native speakers. We have made the dataset and associated code publicly available to support the research community.

The paper introduces Executive Function (EF), a contrastive value policy designed for resampling and relabeling perceptions through hindsight summarization. This approach aims to enhance the generalization capabilities of deep neural networks by addressing their tendency toward overfitting. The study demonstrates that applying EF to a standard ResNet-50 architecture significantly boosts performance on the ImageNet-1K benchmark, achieving 76.1% top-1 accuracy and a 5.1% improvement over the baseline. The authors also present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's theoretical properties, including its convergence behavior, and provide empirical evidence of its robustness against adversarial attacks. The research concludes with a discussion on the broader implications of EF for advancing deep learning research.

Bias in machine learning models can lead to significant performance degradation, particularly in healthcare applications where it may result in unfair treatment of specific groups. While prior research has primarily focused on detecting biases stemming from explicit attributes like age or gender, this study addresses the challenge of identifying biases inherent in data that are not explicitly labeled. We introduce a novel approach to identify such intrinsic biases in medical imaging datasets by leveraging the interplay between image content and model predictions. Our method employs a new metric, the "intrinsic bias score," which quantifies the degree of bias present in a specific dataset. We validate this approach using two medical imaging datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in uncovering latent biases. Furthermore, we illustrate how this metric can guide the development of debiasing strategies to enhance model fairness.

This paper introduces a new loss function for noisy metric learning, designed to enhance the robustness of learned representations against label errors and data augmentation artifacts. By leveraging the geometric properties of the hypersphere method, we develop a smooth approximation of the proxy-anchor loss that maintains computational efficiency. Our extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 0.5% improvement in top-1 accuracy on the CUB dataset.

We introduce a novel statistical technique for analyzing galaxy surveys that leverages density-weighted two-point correlation functions. This approach utilizes the local density environment of galaxies to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio in cosmological parameter estimation. We apply this method to the SDSS-III BOSS DR12 dataset, which comprises a sample of 1.1 million galaxies with redshifts between 0.2 and 0.75. Our analysis yields constraints on the matter density ($\Omega_{\rm m}$) and the amplitude of matter fluctuations ($\sigma_8$) that are consistent with Planck CMB data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our density-weighted correlation functions provide an improvement in cosmological parameter constraints compared to standard, unweighted correlation functions.

This paper investigates the relationship between the sectional genera of a sequence of ideals and their associated local cohomology modules. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any Cohen-Macaulay local ring $R$ with a parameter ideal $I$, the sectional genus of $R/I$ matches the last positive shift in the Betti numbers of the canonical module $\omega_{R/I}$. This finding extends a result previously established by J. Herzog and N. V. Trung for non-Gorenstein rings. Furthermore, we prove that for any Cohen-Macaulay local ring $R$ with a parameter sequence $a_1, \dots, a_d$ and corresponding quotient $R/(a_1, \dots, a_d)$, the sectional genus of this quotient is bounded below by the last positive shift in the Betti numbers of the canonical module $\omega_R$.

This study presents the first nuclear forward scattering (NFS) investigation of the high-pressure magnetic properties of the four-layered Aurivillius phase, $\text{Bi}_5\text{FeTi}_3\text{O}_{15}$. The research reveals that the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions within the $\text{FeO}_6$ octahedra exhibit a spin reorientation transition from a canted antiferromagnetic state to a commensurate antiferromagnetic state at approximately 1.2 GPa. Furthermore, the magnetic moment of the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions is observed to decrease with rising pressure, a trend attributed to the compression of the octahedra.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian framework for ranking brokers' trading algorithms, which integrates algorithm performance, trading costs, and uncertainty. We model the cumulative trading cost as a random variable and employ a Markov chain to represent the sequence of trades within an algorithm. We subsequently develop a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to sample from the posterior distribution of performance metrics. We apply this approach to rank algorithms using Bayesian A/B testing, and we demonstrate the method's effectiveness through a case study on a portfolio of 100 stocks.

We introduce a fully reconfigurable, passive, optomechanical add-drop filter designed to operate in the resolved sideband regime. This device utilizes a ring resonator coupled to a single mechanical resonator, which is in turn interfaced with a bus waveguide. By adjusting the mechanical resonator's frequency, we can dynamically control the filter's transmission spectrum, specifically targeting the resonator-induced sideband anti-Tamm structure. This structure enables tunable control over the filter's transmission amplitude and bandwidth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system can function as a multiplexed filter by selectively addressing multiple sidebands.

This study examines the efficacy of web content analysis in monitoring public health interventions. We introduce a novel method for detecting outbreaks and assessing their severity by leveraging textual data from online sources. The approach employs a weighted term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) weighting scheme to enhance the precision of outbreak detection. Furthermore, we utilize the resulting TF-IDF scores to estimate outbreak intensity. The proposed methodology is validated using a comprehensive dataset of 1.2 million tweets and 1.2 million Google search queries, covering a six-month period. Our findings indicate that the refined method significantly improves outbreak detection accuracy compared to standard TF-IDF approaches.

This paper introduces a neural network designed for lossless image compression that has been thoroughly evaluated on current state-of-the-art benchmarks. The study details the network's architecture, training methodology, and performance outcomes. Notably, the implementation leverages a GPU-end-to-end framework optimized for practical deployment, enabling the processing of images at full resolution. The approach employs a dual-stage structure: the first stage utilizes a global encoder-decoder to capture long-range dependencies, while the second stage applies a convolutional autoencoder to encode local features. The authors demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses existing techniques in performance across various image categories, including natural, synthetic, and medical imagery.

This study reports the first observation of the $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ decay, with a branching fraction of $(1.0 \pm 0.4 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}$, measured using a dataset of 1.0 fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV. Additionally, the analysis searches for $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ decays, finding no significant signal. Consequently, an upper limit on the branching fraction of $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ is established at $1.1 \times 10^{-5}$ at the 95\% confidence level.

Optimal transport (OT) has become a vital tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, yet it is highly susceptible to outliers, which can drastically alter the resulting distance metric. This paper introduces a novel OT framework that maintains robustness against outliers while preserving desirable theoretical properties. Our approach employs a robust loss function that assigns zero cost to extreme deviations, effectively neutralizing their impact on the Wasserstein distance. We demonstrate that this function is statistically robust, possessing a breakdown point of 50% and a high efficiency relative to the Gaussian case. Furthermore, we establish the robustness of the OT barycenter, a critical component in numerous applications. We also present an efficient algorithm for computing the proposed robust transport distance, validated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This paper introduces a new framework designed to enhance human-AI collaboration in decision-making processes. The approach employs reinforcement learning to optimize human behavior within a specific task, aiming to maximize the long-term value of the human-AI team. We present a novel algorithm that integrates the Q-learning algorithm with a generative model of human decision-making. This method is capable of learning the generative model of human decisions and subsequently optimizing human behavior to achieve the highest possible joint value for the human-AI pair. The system is evaluated in a simulated driving scenario, demonstrating its ability to improve the long-term value of the human-AI team.

This review examines the theoretical and phenomenological implications of retaining full supersymmetry in the Higgs sector, specifically focusing on the heavy Higgs bosons that arise when the Higgs sector is extended by additional superfields.

Visualization tools are increasingly utilized to analyze data across diverse fields, including biology, medicine, and engineering. While prior research has examined how specific tasks and visualization types influence performance, the impact of individual differences on these outcomes remains under-explored. This study investigates the role of individual differences in data analysis by comparing task performance across various disciplines. We recruited 120 participants from three distinct fields—medicine, engineering, and biology—to complete a series of data analysis tasks. Results indicate that task performance varies significantly by discipline, with engineers outperforming the other groups. Furthermore, we observed that task success is driven by spatial ability, the type of data, and the specific task involved.

This paper examines the relationship between induction and clause sets cycles. We introduce a novel, simplified definition of induction that is strictly weaker than standard first-order induction yet sufficiently robust to facilitate cycle proofs in specific cases where conventional first-order induction fails.

Graph-based document retrieval has recently gained significant traction, particularly due to the widespread adoption of knowledge graphs. This area focuses on identifying the most relevant documents for a given query by measuring the similarity between a query graph and candidate document graphs. This paper introduces a novel neural architecture designed for graph retrieval, which utilizes a matching model to determine the similarity between query and candidate documents. The proposed method employs a bipartite matching algorithm to align query nodes with nodes from the candidate document graph, thereby establishing a one-to-one correspondence between them. This approach effectively captures the structural relationships between the two graphs. Furthermore, we present a neural framework that integrates a bipartite matching algorithm with a graph neural network to learn a similarity metric for this purpose. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on two benchmark datasets.

This study introduces a novel framework for modeling transient dynamics in complex systems by drawing inspiration from Natural Language Processing (NLP). The approach treats a time series as a sequence of states, utilizing a Transformer architecture to capture the interdependencies between them. We demonstrate that this method is highly effective for both modeling and forecasting, with its performance surpassing that of leading existing techniques. Furthermore, we propose specific training strategies designed to enhance the model's ability to handle rare events.

This paper introduces a framework for allocating electricity across a distribution network, addressing both the physical constraints of the system and the economic realities of the market. The core objective is to distribute power fairly among consumers while strictly adhering to grid limitations and economic conditions. To achieve this, we propose a novel method that integrates established fair division algorithms with power flow analysis. The approach begins by determining the total available generation capacity, followed by an iterative process where consumers sequentially select power from their remaining supply. The method's effectiveness is validated through computational experiments on a real-world distribution network, demonstrating that it successfully balances fairness with technical feasibility.

Event coreference resolution (ECR) identifies narrative links between distinct event mentions, a task that is particularly vital for contentious political contexts where the same incident may be described through varying lenses. This paper introduces a novel dataset comprising 1,000 manually annotated news articles focused on the most recent contentious political occurrences. We also present a novel, unsupervised method for ECR that leverages event type and time information to enhance performance. Evaluated on the newly introduced dataset, our approach achieves an F1 score of 80.1.

This study introduces a novel family of valid inequalities for the complementarity knapsack problem (CKP), a knapsack variant where pairwise product terms enforce complementarity restrictions. Our approach involves lifting previously established inequalities for the underlying knapsack polytope that are valid for specific substructures of CKP, thereby generating a new subclass of facet-defining inequalities. We also detail facets associated with these inequalities and present computational findings supporting the efficacy of these inequalities.

In this paper, we investigate the structure of a standard left identity ring $R$ under the condition that it is semiprime. We specifically examine a generalized $(m, n)$-Jordan derivation $f$ on $R$ that commutes with a specific generalized $(m, n)$ centralizer $g$ on $R$, demonstrating that $f$ must be a generalized $(m, n)$-Jordan inner derivation. Furthermore, we establish that if $R$ is noncommutative and $f$ is a generalized $(m, n)$-Jordan derivation that commutes commutes with a specific generalized $(m, n)$ centralizer $g$ on $R$, then $f$ must be a generalized $(m, n)$-Jordan inner derivation.

We demonstrate that the Weinberg gauge boson two-body decay factor, which is typically derived from spontaneous symmetry breaking, can alternatively be deduced solely from the conservation of gauge symmetry and helicity principles.

We define a transversal family of sets as a collection of subsets within $\mathbb{R}^d$ where the intersection of any two elements has a one-dimensional measure of zero. We demonstrate that if a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ possesses a transversal family of projections onto $d-1$ dimensional linear subspaces, all sharing the same measure, and if one of these projections has finite measure, then $\mu(D)$ is finite for any set $D$ that is also transversal to those subspaces. Furthermore, we establish a generalization of the transversal family concept, termed a "thick" transversal family, and prove a corresponding result for this case. These findings extend and unify several theorems concerning the measure of intersections of projected sets, as well as those concerning the Faverd length of curves.

We introduce a data-efficient algorithm for Guided Policy Search (GPS) that integrates Model Predictive Control (MPC) with imitation learning. This approach is specifically designed to address control tasks where the reward function is either unknown or difficult to define. GPS initially trains a robust dynamics model capable of handling uncertainty, which is then utilized to generate a robust MPC policy. This MPC policy is subsequently imitated to train a guided neural network, which serves as the final policy. This method offers two primary advantages: first, it enables the generation of diverse demonstrations by adjusting MPC parameters, and second, it facilitates the continuous addition of new data to the training set without retraining the dynamics model. Experimental results on a quadruped robot demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms standard GP techniques in terms of reward maximization while requiring significantly less data.

The third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (IAHE) is a recently identified phenomenon occurring in time-reversal-symmetry-broken, inversion-symmetric, and magnetically ordered materials. This study employs a generalized semiclassical framework to derive the IAHE for a broad class of three-dimensional systems, revealing that the effect is determined by the magnetization-dependent third-order Berry curvature dipole (BCD). We demonstrate that this BCD arises from a novel type of Berry curvature multipole moment, which is established by the interplay between non-coplanar spin textures and magnetization. Furthermore, we provide a generalized semiclassical formulation for the BCD, showing that it stems from the interference between two distinct semiclassical mechanisms: the shift current and the side-jump effect.

Call graphs serve as a vital instrument for comprehending the internal workings of software systems. While numerous studies have developed methods to automatically generate call graphs, the analysis of ensembles—collections of these call graphs—remains largely unexplored. This paper introduces an approach to visualize ensembles of call graphs, enabling users to identify patterns and variations across the set. Our methodology involves creating a unified visualization that integrates both the individual call graphs and their interrelationships. We detail the design process of this visualization, the criteria used to select appropriate encodings, and the specific tasks supported by our system. Furthermore, we outline the system's practical application in analyzing call graphs derived from a benchmark dataset comprising 100 software systems.

This study examines the One Billion Word Benchmark (OWB), a widely used resource for evaluating word embeddings, by analyzing its construction process and inherent limitations. We demonstrate that the corpus is heavily biased toward recent news, with a significant overrepresentation of Western media outlets. Furthermore, we show that these media outlets disproportionately publish about the United States, creating a strong geographical bias. We also identify a temporal bias, noting that the dataset is skewed toward the United Kingdom, as it was compiled from the BBC's website. Additionally, we find that the corpus overrepresents the British variant of the English language. These biases are further exacerbated by the fact that the dataset is heavily skewed toward the political left. Consequently, we argue that the dataset is not representative of the global population and that the biases inherent in the data could lead to unfair outcomes when used to evaluate word embeddings.

Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) are a common feature of solar flares, yet their physical origins remain unclear. This study investigates a QPP event occurring during a solar flare on 2014 March 29, utilizing microwave imaging from the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NORH) and simultaneous X-ray data from the Reuven Ramaty High-Energy Solar Spectroscopic Explorer (RHESSI). The analysis reveals that the QPPs manifest as a series of brightening episodes in a compact, elongated source located in the lower part of the flare's current sheet. These bursts are spatially confined to the region of strongest magnetic field intensity. The observed QPPs are characterized by a period of approximately 100 seconds, with peak microwave fluxes ranging from 0.1 to 0.2 Jy. The data indicate that the QPPs are driven by the impulsive release of magnetic energy at the lower current sheet, likely through the repeated formation and collapse of magnetic islands.

This paper introduces a multi-scale anomaly detection method designed for industrial quality inspection. The approach utilizes a contrastive rule-based scoring system to evaluate the degree of anomaly across various scales, employing a multi-kernel convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features at different levels. These multi-scale features are then aggregated to generate a comprehensive anomaly score for each image. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Kramers' theorem asserts that time-reversal symmetric quantum systems with odd particle counts exhibit degeneracy, a principle that can be breached in open systems due to environmental interactions. This study examines such time-reversal symmetric open quantum systems, specifically analyzing how the degeneracy of their eigenvalues changes as a function of dissipation. We demonstrate that under these conditions, eigenvalue splitting can occur, yet the time-reversal symmetry remains intact. Furthermore, we identify a specific parameter regime where eigenvalue revivals take place. These findings are validated through numerical simulations of a two-level quantum system coupled to an environment.

This study introduces a new deep learning framework designed to forecast future Channel State Information (CSI) in high-mobility massive MIMO environments. The proposed method utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to estimate the CSI of the upcoming subframe based on the CSI of the preceding three subframes. By employing the CNN to extract spatial and temporal features from the past three subframes, the system effectively predicts the channel state for the next interval. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing deep learning-based solutions in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) performance.

This study introduces a Bayesian hierarchical model designed to estimate inequality metrics across small areas. The model leverages the Beta mixture distribution to represent the inequality of a variable within each region, accommodating both bounded distributions like the Beta and unbounded ones like the Pareto. We propose a flexible, parsimonious parameterization for the mixture components that facilitates straightforward posterior sampling. The approach is applied to estimate the Gini coefficient for household income across small geographic areas in the United States, with results demonstrating its effectiveness.

We establish a uniform asymptotic expansion for this kernel as the radius of the tube shrinks to zero. This result is significant because it resolves a question raised by Fefferman regarding the existence of such an expansion for non-tube domains. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the leading term of the expansion corresponds to the diagonal values of the Kähler form on the complexified manifold. This paper presents MARINLINGA, a novel algorithm for constructing reverse line graphs from general graphs. Leveraging the matrix-based approach of the Relabeling algorithm, MARINLINGA is designed to operate with linear time complexity relative to the number of edges in the input graph. Its efficacy is demonstrated through comparative analyses with the Roussopoulos algorithm, highlighting its superior performance and providing a robust methodological framework for solving reverse line graph problems.
This article provides a proof of Lee-Lee's conjecture, which addresses the geometric properties associated with the locus of non-rigid indecomposable modules over acyclic quivers.

Java developers frequently encounter bloated dependencies, which are libraries that include unnecessary code, causing the final compiled application to exceed the required size. This issue is particularly prevalent in Java ecosystems, where developers often rely on tools like Maven or Gradle to manage dependencies. This study presents a thorough analysis of such bloated dependencies through a longitudinal examination of 1,000 Java projects. Our findings indicate that bloated dependencies are widespread, with 60% of the affected projects containing at least one instance. Furthermore, we provide a detailed breakdown of the specific characteristics of these instances. Our analysis also reveals that developers often address bloated dependencies by removing them entirely or by utilizing Java compiler options to exclude specific parts. However, our results show that developers frequently fail to address these issues, leaving them unresolved. To aid in this area, we introduce a novel approach for automatically identifying bloated dependencies and their specific instances.

We present a controlled synthesis method for quantum chains utilizing entangled control photons, wherein the kinematic and antagonistic behaviors of classical probability chains are governed by phase relationships between their respective quantum analogs.

This study examines multistage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problems characterized by ambiguity sets constructed from empirical data using a sliding window approach. We introduce a novel set of scenario collections termed "effective scenarios," which are demonstrated to be sufficient for determining the optimal value of such problems. We further prove that these effective scenarios are contained within a specific subset of the ambiguity set known as an "optimal support scenario set." This finding yields a sufficient condition for strong duality applicable to a broad spectrum of multistage DRO formulations. Additionally, we establish that the count of effective scenarios remains bounded by a constant independent of the problem's stage count, thereby offering a theoretical basis for the efficacy of two-stage sliding window scenario collections. Finally, we provide empirical evidence showing that the quality of stochastic programming solutions can be significantly enhanced by restricting the recourse evaluation to these optimal scenario sets.

This study introduces a new deep learning framework designed to predict human actions by anticipating the next movement. The core of this approach is an RNN equipped with a recurrent layer that utilizes radial basis function (RBF) kernels to map feature vectors. The model is trained on a dataset of human motion sequences, where it learns to forecast subsequent frames based on prior observations. The effectiveness of this method was validated through experiments on the NTU RGB-D 120 dataset, where it was benchmarked against existing state-of-the-art techniques. The results indicate that the proposed RNN architecture, which integrates RBF kernel-based feature mapping, significantly outperforms current methods in the field of action anticipation.

We introduce a solvable model for a quantum many-body system featuring a non-thermal steady state, which is achieved by combining a chaotic Hamiltonian with a designated subregion of sites governed by a distinct Hamiltonian. This architecture permits the exploration of how varying timescales between subsystems influence the system's dynamics. Specifically, we demonstrate that when the designated region is initialized in a product state relative to the chaotic sector, the system undergoes rapid thermalization across all other sectors, yet the specified time remains unthermalized. This phenomenon arises because the specific eigenstates of the defined Hamiltonian are effectively "dark," remaining decoupled from the chaotic modes. Furthermore, we show that introducing a slight coupling between the subsystems renders these states bright, thereby facilitating rapid thermalization throughout the system. This framework offers a valuable theoretical foundation for investigating the dynamics of quantum thermalization in scenarios involving disparate timescales.

This study establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions for a symbol to define a nuclear bounded operator on a homogeneous tree. Furthermore, it derives explicit formulas for the matrix elements of such a nuclear operator and investigates the formation of ideal of these operators within the context of complex homogeneous trees.

The fifth generation (5G) of wireless networks is designed to deliver high-speed connectivity and ultra-low latency, serving diverse applications ranging from autonomous vehicles to augmented reality. However, the deployment of 5G infrastructure introduces significant electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure risks for users. This study evaluates the potential EMF exposure resulting from 5G networks by analyzing the spatial distribution of base stations and the propagation of radio waves. The findings indicate that exposure levels are predominantly dominated by the near-field component, which diminishes rapidly with distance. Consequently, the research demonstrates that exposure levels are contingent upon the density of base stations and the specific frequency bands utilized.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. However, these models often exhibit overconfidence when processing out-of-distribution (OOD) data, a phenomenon that poses significant risks in critical sectors like autonomous driving and medical diagnosis. This paper introduces a novel method to address overconfidence in OOD scenarios by leveraging the inherent uncertainty of such data. We propose a novel metric, the Chamfer Out-of-Doin-Example (CODE), which quantifies the average distance between OOD points and the nearest in-distribution (ID) points within the feature space. By incorporating CODE into the loss function, we can effectively penalize the model's excessive certainty regarding OOD inputs. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach substantially mitigates overconfidence issues in OOD detection.

This study presents azimuthal correlations for inclusive 2-jet, 3-jet, and 4-jet events in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, utilizing data from the CMS detector at the LHC. The analysis covers a pseudorapidity range of $|\eta| < 2.4$ for jets with transverse momenta exceeding 30 GeV/$c$. The measured correlation functions are compared against predictions from Monte Carlo event generators and perturbative QCD calculations. Additionally, the study examines the correlation between the scalar sum of jet transverse momenta and the normalized azimuthal difference between the two leading jets. The observed data are also benchmarked against next-to-leading order pQCD predictions.

Deep learning has achieved significant success in numerous computer vision tasks, yet the majority of existing methods depend on large volumes of labeled data. In contrast, semi-supervised and unsupervised learning approaches aim to reduce the need for extensive annotations by utilizing unlabeled data. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of recent advancements in deep unsupervised and semi-supervised learning for computer vision. We begin by examining the application of deep unsupervised techniques to diverse areas, including image classification, representation learning, and image generation. Subsequently, we explore various strategies for semi-supervised learning, such as consistency regularization, pseudo-labeling, and self-training. Finally, we conclude the paper by discussing open challenges and potential future research directions within semi-supervised and unsupervised learning.

Outlier detection is a critical task in data mining, yet most existing methods struggle with high-dimensional datasets. This paper introduces RECol, a novel approach that mitigates the curse of dimensionality by generating reconstruction error columns. The method employs a denoising autoencoder to derive these columns, which are subsequently used to train a one-class SVM for outlier identification. Experimental results demonstrate that RECol outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in detecting outliers within high-dimensional data.

This study examines a non-linear stochastic differential equation driven by a non-degenerate Brownian motion, where the drift coefficient depends on the Young integral of that drift with respect to the solution itself. We establish that this problem admits a unique solution that is $C^{\infty}$-smooth, provided the drift's dependence on the auxiliary variable is sufficiently regular. Furthermore, we derive uniform estimates for the solution and its derivatives across all probability spaces. We also present an example demonstrating that the established framework applies to a specific stochastic ordinary differential equation (SDE) featuring a singular drift.

We investigate the polarizability of neutrinos, a phenomenon that arises when neutrinos are surrounded by matter. This study examines how this property varies with the energy of the neutrinos and the specific conditions of the matter environment.

This study examines the dynamics of a neuronal-glial network using a mean-field framework. The model incorporates glial cells as a source of excitatory stimuli for neurons, while simultaneously absorbing inhibitory signals from them. By applying a self-consistent approach, we derive the probability density function for neuronal membrane potential, which allows for the calculation of the firing rate. The resulting bifurcation analysis reveals that the system undergoes a saddle-node on limit cycle (SNLC) transition, leading to the emergence of self-sustained oscillations. Furthermore, we identify a second bifurcation point associated with a Hopf limit cycle (Hopf), which marks the boundary of the parameter region where stable oscillations occur.

We investigate the topological properties of a neutral spin-1/2 particle situated in a spatially varying magnetic field, focusing on the topological phase diagram of its ground state. This diagram is constructed using the non-Abelian Chern number and the Abelian winding number, both derived from the system's Berry curvature and Berry connection, respectively. We demonstrate that the non-Abelian Chern number corresponds to the sum of the winding numbers associated with each energy band. Furthermore, we establish that the system's ground state exhibits non-trivial topology, characterized by a Berry phase of $2\pi$. This topological structure arises from the specific configuration of the magnetic field and the spin degree of freedom of the particle.

This study examines the retraction of a moving boundary in a diffusion process, where the movement is governed by the arrival time of the diffusion at a specific point, known as the first-passage time. We establish that, under certain conditions, this retraction can accelerate exponentially over time. We further demonstrate applications involving standard Brownian motion and the square Bessel process.

This paper examines the formal semigroups of L-space knots within the context of hyperbolic geometry. We present a comprehensive enumeration of these formal semigroups for hyperbolic L-space knots that exhibit small values of $g_{\rm hyperbolic} - g_{\rm L}$. Furthermore, we establish that formal semigroups are invariant under quasi-isometry for such knots when the specified $g_{\rm hyperbolic} - g_{\rm L}$ difference is minimal.

This work examines the connection between the kinetic theory of gases and hydrodynamic models for compressible flows. We establish a Poisson mapping linking the collisionless Boltzmann equation to a specific Hamiltonian system of Euler-type equations. The resulting hydrodynamic model differs from the standard Euler equations by allowing entropy to vary spatially. Furthermore, we establish that this entropy distribution adheres to a first-order transport equation. Finally, we demonstrate the validity of the classical Boltzmann-Grad limit for the collisionless system, yielding the desired Euler-type equations.

This study introduces a novel ensemble methodology designed to enhance the robustness of endoscopic video artifact detection. The approach leverages a diverse collection of detectors, including both state-of-the-art models and those specifically fine-tuned for the task, by employing a voting scheme to establish a consensus on the presence of artifacts. This voting mechanism is further refined by incorporating a custom weighting strategy that accounts for the reliability of individual detectors. Experimental results indicate that this ensemble method surpasses the performance of standalone detectors, achieving a 9.0% reduction in false positive rates and a 1.0% improvement in true positive rates.

Identifiers are fundamental to source code, serving as the primary mechanism for naming variables, functions, and classes. While developers often rely on naming conventions to grasp code intent, these patterns can also be exploited to automate code generation and analysis. This study examines the patterns of identifier names found in Java, Python, and JavaScript, revealing that although each language exhibits distinct characteristics, they share core structural and semantic traits. We introduce a novel methodology for modeling these patterns, which enables the automatic creation of grammars tailored to specific languages. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these grammar models can be utilized to assess the semantic correctness of identifiers, thereby supporting code generation and static analysis tasks.

We construct a Fock space representation of a quantum vertex algebra associated with affine $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$, utilizing a Fuchsian differential equation linked to a Riemann-Hilbert problem. This approach yields an infinite-dimensional irreducible highest weight module for the quantum vertex algebra, characterized by an arbitrary complex structure on its lowest weight.

Grain growth is a critical factor in the microstructural evolution of polycrystalline materials, and its analysis typically relies on the grain-size distribution (GSD). This study introduces a novel approach to modeling grain growth by utilizing the GSD to determine the probability density function (PDF) of grain growth rates. The proposed method is applied to duplex and triplex systems, where the former involves a single growth rate and the latter involves two distinct rates. The analysis demonstrates that grain growth kinetics can be effectively characterized by a single rate, provided the system is duplex. However, in triplex configurations, the growth rates are distributed across two populations. This distribution arises because the initial grain-size distribution is bimodal, and the resulting grain-size distribution is a superposition of two distinct distributions, each corresponding to a specific growth rate.

This study introduces a new benchmark for human pose and shape estimation, which is the first to evaluate 3D human pose estimation algorithms across diverse conditions, including variations in lighting, occlusion, and object scale. We also present a detailed analysis of the benchmark's characteristics and the performance of state-of-the-art methods under these challenging scenarios. Our findings indicate that existing approaches struggle significantly with these specific conditions, suggesting that future research must prioritize robustness in these areas.

We introduce a model-independent effective action designed to facilitate the matching of lepton flavor violating (LFV) observables between low- and high-energy frameworks, specifically within the context of a scalar lepton-quark (LQ) model. This approach is particularly valuable for analyzing LFV phenomena that cannot be adequately explained by the Standard Model. We demonstrate that integrating this model-independent action with specific LQ models yields precise predictions for relevant observables. Furthermore, we examine the efficacy of decoupling in the context of the lepton universality ratio $R_{K^{(*)}}$.

Machine learning has become a cornerstone of modern computer science, with deep learning serving as a particularly influential subfield. This research focuses on the compositional aspects of machine learning, utilizing category theory as a framework to model these systems. We examine the compositional structure of deep learning architectures and extend this analysis to include convolutional neural networks. Furthermore, we explore the composability of convolutional layers within the context of convolutional neural networks.

This study introduces a novel optimal finite-time control method designed for second-order dynamic systems. By employing a fractional power function for the terminal state error, the proposed controller ensures precise asymptotic tracking of reference trajectories. The control parameters are derived from a newly defined optimal cost function, which is formulated based on the terminal error and its derivative. Furthermore, the paper presents a robust, chattering-free implementation of this optimal finite-time control strategy.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are critical for the transition to sustainable energy, yet their manufacturing involves intricate, multi-layered architectures that are difficult to inspect using traditional methods. To address this, we propose a non-destructive ultrasonic technique capable of characterizing the entire battery. By analyzing the resonance frequencies of a coin cell, we successfully determined the thicknesses of its constituent layers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the speed of sound within the electrode material can be derived from the resonance spectrum, offering a means to assess the state of charge. This study establishes a foundation for developing advanced ultrasonic tools to probe the internal structure of LIBs, which could significantly enhance both manufacturing processes and the operational safety of these devices.

This paper introduces a discrete-time flatness-based control method for gantry cranes, a framework that encompasses both linear and nonlinear models. The approach enables the simultaneous regulation of the payload and the gantry, while also providing an efficient technique for trajectory generation. Theoretical findings are substantiated through simulation results.

Image captioning involves generating textual descriptions for input images. While deep learning has significantly advanced this field, the scarcity of large-scale annotated datasets remains a primary obstacle to further progress. To address this, we introduce a cooperative distillation framework that leverages unlabeled data to enhance performance. Our approach utilizes a student-teacher architecture, where the student model learns from the teacher's predictions. To ensure the student generalizes effectively to unseen data, we incorporate a knowledge distillation loss alongside a standard cross-entropy loss. Additionally, we implement a curriculum learning strategy to optimize training efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques on the MS-COCO dataset.

A collection of strings is defined as well-connected if every pair of strings within it can be transformed into one another via a sequence of strings that all remain part of the collection. This paper investigates the structural characteristics of well-connected sets, specifically demonstrating that any well-connected set of binary strings with length $n$ must contain at least $n$ elements. Furthermore, we establish that the minimal binary well-connected set of length $n$ consists of exactly $n$ elements, whereas the minimal non-binary well-connected set of length $n$ requires only $n-1$ elements. We also prove that any non-binary well-connected set of length $n$ with fewer than $n+1$ elements contains precisely one non-empty subsequence of length $n-1$. Finally, we show that the minimal non-binary well-connected set of length $n$ is unique and consists of a specific construction involving $n-1$ elements.

Ehresmann semigroups are defined as semirectangles composed of an inverse semigroup and a semigroup with a distinguished idempotent. This paper establishes the theory of orderings for these structures by extending existing concepts from inverse semigroups. Specifically, we demonstrate that the partial orders inherent in an Ehresmann semigroup are completely determined by its identity component (inverse subsemigroup) and its right group of units. Furthermore, we examine the connection between these natural orders and those canonical orders found in inverse semigroups and right groups separately. Finally, we outline the fundamental properties of ordered Ehresmann semigroups.

Self-attention mechanisms have become a cornerstone of modern deep learning, driving significant advancements across various domains. While the efficacy of these models is widely recognized to depend on their architectural dimensions, the specific relationship between their depth (number of layers) and width (number of heads) remains poorly understood. This paper investigates how depth and width interact in self-attention architectures, demonstrating that the depth-to-width ratio is a critical factor in determining model performance. We provide a theoretical analysis of the information capacity within self-attention mechanisms and show that this capacity scales with the width-to-depth ratio. Furthermore, we conduct an empirical study on the impact of these architectural choices on self-attention's ability to learn, revealing that the dynamics of the depth-to-width ratio are essential for optimizing model performance.

This study details the creation of BiFeO$_{3}$ nanoparticles (BNOs) with a particle size of 10 nm using a sol-gel method at cryogenic temperatures. The synthesized BNOs were characterized via X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and UV-Vis spectroscopy. Results indicate that the material is a single-phase hexagonal perovskite with a hexagonal crystal structure, exhibiting a hexagonal lattice constant of 0.38 nm. Notably, the sample displays a room-temperature magnetization of 0.12 emu/g, a value significantly higher than those reported for other BNOs. Furthermore, the material demonstrates promising photocatalytic activity, evidenced by a 90% degradation of Rhodamine B dye and a hydrogen evolution rate of 100 $\mu$mol h$^{-1}$ g$^{-1}$ under visible light irradiation. These findings suggest that the low-temperature synthesis approach is highly effective for producing BNOs with superior magnetic and photocatalytic properties.

This study introduces a novel approach for reconstructing generic objects held in human hands, a task that is both challenging and essential for applications like robotic manipulation and augmented reality. We achieve this by utilizing a single RGB image to simultaneously reconstruct the 3D geometry of the object and the pose of the hands gripping it. Our method employs a two-stage process: first, a hands-only segmentation isolates the grasping area from the background; second, a dedicated network reconstructs the object's geometry based on this isolated hand region. We introduce the OpenHands3D dataset, comprising 10,000 synthetic images of objects in various poses within hands, which includes ground truth data for segmentation, camera parameters, and 3D models. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The Ca II K spectral line serves as a primary indicator of chromospheric activity in the Sun and other stars. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the Ca II K index and chromospheric activity features using a century-long dataset spanning 1919 to 2019, derived from 1,000 nights of observations at the Kodaikanal Observatory. To ensure data consistency, we developed a consistent contrast algorithm that was rigorously validated against the AARON database. Our investigation reveals that the Ca II K index exhibits a strong correlation with the 11-year solar cycle, with a correlation coefficient of 0.97. Furthermore, we identified a significant correlation between the Ca II K index and the Wolf sunspot number (R=0.97), as well as the 10.7 cm radio flux (R=0.95). Additionally, we examined the relationship between the Ca II K index and the Wolf sunspot number across various solar activity levels, finding that the correlation coefficient increases from 0.90 during low activity to 0.95 during high activity. Finally, we compared the Ca II K index with the Wolf sunspot number and found that the correlation coefficient increases from 0.90 during low activity to 0.95 during high activity.

The study presents the first observation of the rare decay $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$, reported using $pp$ collision data from the LHCb experiment with an integrated luminosity of $3.0~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected at a centre-of-mass energy of $7~\mathrm{TeV}$. The measured branching fraction is $(1.71 \pm 0.31(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.21(\mathrm{sys})) \times 10^{-10}$, which aligns with Standard Model predictions. Additionally, the analysis investigates the $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay angular distribution and the $\Lambda \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay, the latter of which is the first measurement of its kind at LHCb.

Symbolic execution is a promising method for uncovering software bugs, yet scaling it to large-scale systems remains difficult. This paper introduces a distributed symbolic execution framework designed to address these challenges. We propose a test-depth partitioning strategy that divides the program's execution space into separate paths for concurrent exploration across multiple processes. To ensure scalability, we developed a distributed constraint solver capable of resolving satisfiability issues across paths executed simultaneously. We implemented this approach in a prototype and evaluated it on two substantial open-source projects, demonstrating that our method successfully uncovers bugs in large-scale software.

We investigate the relaxation dynamics of magnetization in chains of magnetic nanoparticles, where the process is governed by the interplay between exchange forces and magnetic anisotropy. By utilizing a model that incorporates both effects, we derive an analytical solution for the time-dependent magnetization. This solution is expressed as a weighted sum of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, where the specific weights depend on the initial magnetization state. We demonstrate that the relaxation behavior is characterized by a two-stage process: an initial rapid decay followed by a slow, long-term relaxation. Furthermore, we establish that the timescale of this prolonged relaxation is determined by the lowest non-zero eigenvalue. Finally, we derive an approximate formula for this eigenvalue, which reveals that the relaxation time varies with the magnitude of the applied magnetic field according to a power law.

Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning framework that enables clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing their private data. While traditional FL systems rely on a central server to aggregate models, this architecture creates a single point of failure and a privacy risk where the server could access client information. To address these limitations, we introduce a decentralized FL approach that aggregates models directly between clients via a trusted social network. This design eliminates the need for a central server by leveraging existing trust relationships, thereby enhancing both the system's resilience and data privacy. We propose a novel method for identifying a social network subgraph that maximizes the number of clients participating in the global model training. Furthermore, we develop a distributed algorithm to identify this optimal subgraph, which is proven to converge to the ideal solution. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a 10% to 20% increase in accuracy compared to existing methods.

This study introduces a sequential short-text classification model that leverages the inherent order of words by integrating recurrent and convolutional neural networks. The recurrent neural network (RNN) processes the linear sequence of tokens to generate a context-aware representation, while the convolutional neural network (CNN) extracts salient features from this representation to produce a final classification. We evaluated the proposed approach on the AG News and IMDB sentiment datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results with 84.5% accuracy on AG News and 90.1% accuracy on the IMDB sentiment dataset.

Fabry-P\'erot (FP) etalons are essential components in numerous astronomical instruments, including high-resolution spectrographs, coronagraphs, and polarimeters. These devices are typically categorized as either telecentric or non-telecentric. This study focuses on deriving the transmission function for telecentric FP etalons, which are characterized by flat, parallel plates. We establish a general transmission function that accounts for the varying angle of incidence of incoming light and the resulting interference patterns. By applying a first-order approximation, we derive a simplified transmission function that facilitates the calculation of the etalon's free spectral range (FSR) and the peak positions of its transmission peaks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this first-order model can be extended to higher orders, thereby enabling precise modeling of the transmission function for any FP etalon configuration.

This work examines the compatibility problem, which seeks to identify a maximum-size matching in a graph $G$ that shares no edges with any matching in a specified subgraph $H \subseteq G$. We demonstrate that determining this problem is NP-complete even when $H$ is restricted to a matching of size two. Furthermore, we establish an upper bound on the maximum number of edges in compatible matchings for graphs with $n$ vertices and a fixed subgraph $H$, alongside proving an asymptotically tight lower bound. Additionally, the study establishes an asymptotically tight lower bound for the situation where $H$ is a star. Finally, the paper presents an efficient algorithm capable of approximating compatible matchings within a constant factor.

Chiplets represent a novel approach to designing integrated circuits, where a single die is partitioned into multiple smaller units, each fabricated on its own substrate and interconnected to form a complete chip. This methodology offers significant advantages, including reduced costs, enhanced flexibility, and improved resilience against manufacturing defects. This paper introduces a formal model for codelets, which are defined as the fundamental building blocks of these chiplets. Codelets are designed to be composable, allowing them to be combined into larger components that can themselves be assembled into chiplets. Furthermore, the text outlines the necessary conditions for ensuring that the resulting chiplet designs are fault-tolerant.

Mixture cure models are widely utilized in survival analysis to address censored data arising from chronic diseases. While recent literature has introduced semiparametric extensions of these models to relax rigid parametric constraints, they often demand intricate estimation procedures. This paper proposes semiparametric cure models that employ a semiparametric framework for baseline hazards and applies presmoothing techniques to estimate the cure proportion function. The resulting estimator is straightforward to compute, exhibits asymptotic normality, and achieves the optimal convergence rate. Furthermore, extensive simulation studies and a real-data analysis are provided to validate the proposed methodology.

The nonlocal metric dimension of a graph $G$, denoted as $d_{f}(G)$, is defined as the smallest integer $k$ for which there exists a dominating set $S \subseteq V(G)$ of size $k$ such that every vertex in $G \setminus S$ is uniquely identified by its distances to the vertices in $S$. This paper establishes upper bounds for $d_{f}(G)$ across various graph types, including trees, unicyclic graphs, bicyclic graphs, and general graphs. Furthermore, it determines the precise nonlocal metric dimension for complete graphs, star graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and specific bicyclic graphs.

In-memory computing (IMC) architectures are emerging as a promising solution to overcome the memory wall, which is caused by the widening performance gap between processors and memory. However, this shift to novel hardware architectures introduces new security challenges, including vulnerabilities to side-channel attacks. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of potential side-channel threats within IMC systems. We begin by reviewing the fundamental principles of IMC and the specific side-channel attack vectors applicable to them. Subsequently, we evaluate the efficacy of countermeasures designed to mitigate these threats. Finally, we propose a novel side-channel attack targeting IMC architectures, demonstrating that such attacks can successfully recover plaintext data from these systems.

We introduce a new class of polarization kernels derived from shortened cyclic codes. These shortened kernels offer significant advantages, including excellent polarization performance and an efficient algorithm for generating them. Their application extends to the construction of space-time codes, where they are utilized to develop codes for the 4×4 MIMO system using 16-QAM. The resulting performance is competitive with existing solutions, notably matching the capabilities of the well-known Alamouti-based 8-QAM codes.

This study introduces a self-supervised deep learning approach for seismic denoising that operates without labeled data and utilizes blind spots in the network architecture. The method involves training a convolutional autoencoder on a dataset of clean seismic traces, followed by the training of a second network on a subset of the original traces, excluding the designated blind areas. During inference, the denoising process is performed on the complete seismic trace by sequentially applying the trained networks to the clean and noisy data within the blind spots. This technique was evaluated on a synthetic dataset comprising 100 clean seismic traces, each containing 1000 samples, with 100 added noise traces. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces noise while preserving the essential features of the seismic traces.

This study examines the charge-asymmetric correlations in the energy of real photons emitted during lepton-proton and antilepton-proton elastic scattering. The analysis utilizes the soft-photon approximation, which is valid for photon energies much lower than the center-of-mass energy. The findings demonstrate that these correlations are sensitive to the incoming particles' charge, specifically highlighting the differences between electron-proton and positron-proton scattering. Additionally, the results indicate that such charge dependence can be observed in the differential cross-sections for real photon emission, particularly when the scattering angle is close to $90^\circ$.

The spin-orbit-coupled Mott insulator Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ exhibits a complex electronic structure characterized by a significant spin-orbit gap, which is typically modeled using a Hubbard-like framework. However, recent findings indicate that this gap is substantially smaller than anticipated, suggesting that the system's behavior is heavily influenced by spin-polaron effects. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of spin-polaron dynamics in Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ using scanning tunneling spectroscopy. We observe that the tunneling spectrum displays a pronounced spin-polarson resonance peak, which is well-explained by a model incorporating spin-polarson formation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the tunneling spectrum is highly sensitive to the spin-polarson binding energy, which is found to be approximately 0.1 eV. These results underscore the critical role of spin-polarson effects in governing the electronic properties of Sr$_2$IrO$_4$.

Estimating causal effects across direct and indirect pathways is frequently complicated by confounding variables and the use of multiple treatments. This study introduces a multiply robust estimation framework for mediation analysis within contexts featuring continuous exposures, extending the previously developed point and set multiple robust approaches for single treatments. We demonstrate that the proposed method remains valid under multiply robust conditions, where at least one specific model among several is correctly specified. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting point estimates and confidence intervals maintain robustness even when multiple relevant models are correctly specified. To facilitate this, we develop a weighted augmentation technique for the indirect effect and a weighted augmentation strategy for the total effect, both of which are grounded in point multiple robustness. Additionally, we propose a robust variance estimation method utilizing a weighted augmentation score function. We further introduce a set multiple robust testing procedure for mediation effects, which is constructed based on the maximum of the proposed point estimate and its corresponding confidence interval. Simulation studies confirm that the method achieves satisfactory performance, and we apply it to analyze the causal mediation effects in data from the National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979.

This study introduces Robin, an online corpus comprising 1.2 million texts from individuals expressing suicidal ideation. The collection was gathered via a dedicated web portal that facilitated the submission of these posts by users. The dataset encompasses a diverse range of content, including forum discussions, comments, blog entries, and social media updates, sourced from platforms such as Reddit, Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube. The research evaluates the performance of various models designed for suicide risk detection, comparing their results against a prior corpus, Hopeless. The findings indicate that the Hopeless dataset is more suitable for training and testing purposes, largely due to its superior quality and more consistent label distribution.

In these models, the scalar field $\phi$ mapping the worldsheet to the target space is governed by a first-order Lagrangian, with the Schwarzian action emerging as a special instance. This study examines the regularity of solutions for the difference equation $x_{n+1}=ax^\alpha_{n}+bx^\alpha_{n-1}$, where $0<\alpha\leq 2$. We establish that the solution remains bounded under specific conditions on the parameters $a$ and $b$, whereas it becomes unbounded when those conditions are not met. Furthermore, we apply this theoretical framework to a medical model describing the dynamics of a single population subject to a time-delayed harvesting strategy.

This study examines a family of nonlinear electrodynamics models that extend the standard Born-Infeld theory, incorporating the Born-Infeld Lagrangian as a specific instance. We introduce a new class of nonlinear models characterized by a parameter $\alpha$, which serves as a deformation of the Born-Infeld case. The analysis focuses on the properties of nonlinear charge and energy within the context of asymptotically flat, static, and charged black hole solutions. We demonstrate that the total energy of these black holes is determined by the sum of the horizon area and the electric charge. Furthermore, we investigate the thermodynamic stability of these black hole solutions.

An $s$-tuple of variables $(x_1, \dots, x_s)$ is designated as a solution to $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_k$ if $\ell_i(x_1, \dots, x_s)$ yields a non-zero integer value for every $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$. A set $A$ is defined as a Sidon set for these linear forms if all solutions to $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_k$ that map distinct $s$-tuples to the same output are necessarily equivalent under a permutation of those variables. This paper establishes that for any collection of $k$ linear forms, a subset of the integers with size $N$ contains at most $O(N^{k/(k+1)})$ collisions.
